titulo: Acer Nitro V 16S Review
transcricao: With me is ASUS's brand new Nitro V16S. Basically, it's their first slim gaming laptop priced to compete in that allimportant value range. MSRP of around $1,200 for the 5060 version to 1,400 for the 5070. It's got a similar chassis to its more expensive and more powerful older brother, the Predator Helios Neo6s. But ASA has done some more money-saving things with this Nitro. It's got an older generation CPU, either one of Intel's Raptor Lake processors, the Core 7240H, or one of AMD's older Zen 4 ones, the Ryzen 7260. It's also missing a Thunderbolt port on the back, which the Predator does have. Its Ethernet port is only 1 gig, not 2.5, and its mechanical trackpad is worse. The Nitros, it seems to dip down more in the left and right corner, making it feel cheaper. And on cheaper, it displays lid, it just feels very flimsy. Lastly, the lowerc cost models of the Nitro V16s, they do have lower resolution 1920 displays. The more expensive ones, they still have a 2560 panel. But guys, none of this matters. You see, the moment we unboxed the Nitro, we noticed a big issue. Its charger, it is tiny, 135 W. We recently reviewed the Yoga Prone, it has similar hardware with a beefier 170 W charger. Well, during gaming on its highest performance mode, we noticed that it drains its battery while plugged in. Many viewers were really frustrated and Lenovo they rushed out of BAS update. That update allows you to pair their larger 245W charger available for their Legion gaming laptops with the Yoga Pro 9i, therefore solving this issue. But you can see where I'm going here. This Nitro has a much smaller 135 W charger. We've never seen anything that low in a mid-range gaming laptop. Even HP's 14-inch Omen transcend 14, which was lambasted for having a low wattage dedicated GPU, has a larger 140 watt charger. This Nitro feeds its dedicated GPU more wattage than the Omen transcend, 85 W versus 75, yet it has a smaller charger. The math, it just doesn't add up for the Nitro, especially when you consider that both the Yoga Pronei and the Omen Transcend use one of Intel's latest Aerolake HPUs. These are much more power efficient than the older Raptor Lake processors in our Nitro V16s. So clearly alarm bells were ringing. Our lead tester, Seth, put together a couple of graphs to demonstrate how bad this issue is. Over two runs of the Forza Horizon 5 benchmark, which takes around 3 minutes in total, this laptop drains over 1% of its battery. That's when it's on its highest performance mode called turbo. Set another way, if you plugged in the Nitro to the wall gained for 5 hours, it would probably just switch off as its battery would be completely drained or its performance would have to be significantly throttled. If you switch down to its performance mode, which feeds it CPU 10 W less during gaming, the battery it still drains, but not nearly as much. Now, this may not sound that bad, but Forza, it's really not the most demanding game in 2025. So, let's take a look at Monster Hunter Wilds, the benchmark. That takes around 6 minutes to run. Here, the Nitro drains more than 2% of its battery when plugged into the wall. A little more than Forza. If you extrapolate this out after 4 hours or so of gaming, your laptop is done. Now, this might not sound like this laptop is a complete no-go. How often do you play games consistently for 4 to 5 hours? Probably not a lot. But as you know, the more you drain and recharge these lithium-ion batteries, the less charge they hold. So in the future, that max gaming session could go down to say 2 to three hours. And degrading your battery will affect your laptop outside of gaming. Say you just want to unplug the laptop and use it around the office or a classroom. If you've used a lot of battery cycles from gaming and recharging, it won't last as long as a laptop without this issue. When we compare the Nitro's battery drain to other laptops, you can see it is by far the worst we've seen with this issue. We thought the Yoga Pro 9 was bad. It's nowhere near as bad as this laptop. By the way, keep in mind the following with our graphs. We didn't start each test when the laptop was fully charged. That's why you see some different starting points. Also, the Y-axis, it doesn't go right down to zero. So, the slope of the line looks worse than if it did. But keep in mind, these tests are really short, between 3 and 6 minutes. So, the same applies to the X-axis. If we ran the test for longer, you'd see the line go down even if the Y-axis went right down to zero. Now, ASA, they're great partners and they do produce some of the best gaming laptops. So, we of course reached out to them and they said that they're looking into this, but to get ahead of a potential solution, we tried the Predator's much larger 230 W charger with this Nitro. The Nitro, it didn't draw any additional power. My guess is similar to the Yoga Prei, ASA needs to release a BIOS update to enable higher wattage charges. This is a little unfortunate. Look, our goal here is to help you find the best laptop for your specific use case. In the case of this laptop, the Nitro V16S, I just can't see a lot of people watching a full review and going, "Hey, I want to buy this laptop." Even with its battery drain issue. So, in a situation like this, I think it makes more sense to just abandon this review. post a link to our test results below, which I've done, and suggest alternate laptop recommendations, which I'm about to do. We can then invest the time that we would have spent finishing this review on getting your review of the next laptop even faster. If ASA fixes the issue, we can always come back to this laptop with the rest of the review. Guys, this is the first time we've taken this approach and just abandoned a review. And I'd like to know from you, what do you think? Do you think it's still worth to do a full review of a laptop like this with such a gating issue? When it comes to what you should buy if you are shopping for a laptop like the Nitro V16S, everyone here thinks that the Legion 5 or 5i is just the way to go. It is Lenovo's 15-inch mid-range gaming laptop. And guys, it is amazing. As you probably seen in our graphs, the Legion 5i, it doesn't drain its battery while plugged in. It feeds its GPU more power. It has a more modern and more powerful CPU. It has a stunning OLED display, Lenovo's amazingly comfortable keyboard, and it's built really well. We have a full review coming out on the Legion 5 with AMD that is and the 5i with Intel, which we can now move faster on because we're abandoning this review. So, get subscribed for that with the notification bell on. If you instead want a 16-in laptop at this price point that competes more head-to-head with the Nitro V, we feel that the Gigabyte Aero X16 just gives you more. It feeds its GPU the same 85 W as the Nitro, but its battery drain is nowhere near as bad. That's because it comes with a larger 150 W charger and it has a much more power efficient current gen AMD Zen 5 CPU. It even lasts longer than the Nitron battery. All SKs of the Arrow that we've seen do have a higher resolution display too, not just the top ones. Even its trackpad feels better. Its build quality though is still pretty mid like the Nitros. In fact, its main issue is that its keyboard deck does have a lot of give to it, so the typing experience it feels mushy. Also, its ports are really far forward and may get in your way. It's especially bad if you're a left-hander, as the power cord, it sticks right out. Anyway, I've done a full review of that laptop, which I will link below. If you want more specific recommendations, then definitely check out our website, bestlaptop.deals. We show you the pros and cons of each laptop that we've reviewed. We show you who we think it's ideal for. We call out when its price makes it a good or great deal. We even have custom price drop notifications that you can set by clicking the bell icon. We've really tried to build a hub for laptop buying and I hope you enjoy using it. I must say it's been a bit of a rough year for Asus so far. Their gaming laptops are hitting the market way late. The Predator Helios Neo6s, which is a really good gaming laptop, also has a pretty big issue. It can't lower its screen's refresh rate down to 60 Hz, so its battery life sucks. titulo: Asus Zenbook 14 & 14X - The BEST Laptop to Buy Right Now ... It's NOT even close
transcricao: the Asus sandbox 14 and 14x are great laptops and in this video I'm not only going to show you why but I'm also going to explain why the 14x in particular is a groundbreaking device I know that's a bold statement but I believe it is one of the most important laptops that has been released in the last several years and yes even Apple needs to be super concerned about this device so let's get into it when you look at the two laptops the Asus Zenbook 14 is noticeably smaller and lighter at 3.1 pounds although not the lightest 14 inch laptop that I've tested I'd still consider it very portable size-wise it's about the same physical size as a MacBook Pro 14 and larger than an air 13 with M2 the 14x is noticeably larger and less portable its weight is similar to the MacBook Pro 14s which is good given it has a larger 14.5 inch screen versus the max 14.2 however due to that larger screen it is physically bigger than the MacBook Pro 14. the lid of the 14 is minimal in its design with just a single Asus logo the 14x though has some cool abstract lines the hinge of the 14 lifts the laptop slightly off the table for better airflow and cooling the 14x already sits a bit above a desk due to its large rubber feet this left design of the 14 makes its keyboard deck not as sturdy as the 14x overall though both laptops do feel very well built but they are not in the same league as a Macbook or a Razer in terms of sturdiness and overall build quality for example when you run your fingers along the bottom edge of either laptop you'll notice the back panel is not totally flush with the rest of the laptop both laptops have great displays stunning OLED panels with excellent color reproduction that is good enough for professional color work they both have that desirable 16 by 10 aspect ratio so you see a little more content for applications that go down the page and they both are decently high resolution at 2880 by 1800 pixels however there are some differences that you must be aware of the Zenbook 14 has a 14 inch display whereas the Zenbook 14x has a larger 14 0.5 both are bright displays although the 14x is a little brighter at 380 nits whereas the smaller 14 hits 360. as a point of reference I would consider 400 nits bright in 2023 side by side though the display of the 14x looks noticeably better the whites look wider and it looks brighter than the measurements show we originally thought that this was due to the display's white balance but we read similar Kelvin readings on both displays our hypothesis is that it's due to a difference in the pre-installed color profiles while we were digging around we did notice that the 14's display supports 10 bit color whereas the 14xs only supports eight both displays are fast refresh rate panels so movement on screen looks smooth however the 14 only offers a 90 Hertz refresh rate and the 14x offers a faster 120 hertz at the end of the day what's actually important is the amount of information you can see on screen without needing to squint this is determined by many aspects of the display that I just mentioned to test this I opened Excel and found that I could comfortably see 37 rows on the Zenbook 14 and 40 rows on the 14x this isn't the best result for the Zenbook 14. most people will appreciate the extra information that they'll see on the 14x one downside of most OLED panels is that they do employ PW and flickering to lower the brightness I.E they turn on and off the panel very quickly so it seems dimmer on the 14 we could only detect this on low brightness settings but on the 14x it was detectable at almost all brightness settings other than the max brightness both laptops have excellent Port selection and they are almost identical if you get one with an Intel processor the two USB C ports will be fast Thunderbolt 4 ones unfortunately if you get an AMD model these are the slower 3.2 Gen 2 10 gigabit ones other than that on the right side both have a fast HDMI 2.1 port and a headphone mic combo Jack the smaller zen14 also has a Micro SD card reader on the left side you've got a fast 10 gigabit Legacy USB a port one thing I don't like is that both charging cable reports are on the right side if your outlet is on the left side you'll have to run a power cable around the back which may get in your way the typing experience on both laptops is excellent top tier the keys have a very satisfying click to them and the keyboard layout is standard so you won't have any annoying Miss hits like you do on keyboards with odd layouts I even like how the power button is one key in from the top of the function row this way the more commonly used delete key is where it should be some laptops have the power button in this position which can cause some mispresses also page up down home and end keys are built into the arrow keys as secondary functions and both keyboards are fully backlit the trackpads on both laptops are good enough tracking is smooth and accurate and clicking Works reasonably well especially as these laptops have mechanical clicking mechanisms normally for these kind of track pads when you click in the bottom left and right Corners you lose accuracy overall though the click it just doesn't have quite that natural feel as you'd get on a MacBook and both laptops do support the Asus number pad in trackpad we found with a light touch it worked pretty well let's take a look at performance the Zenbook 14 that I have has a ryzen 7730u processor it uses amd's incredibly confusing and totally misleading naming convention the first digit being 7 means it was released in 2023 but it actually uses the Zen 3 architecture from a prior year which you can tell by the third digit being a three it's also a u-series processor so it is aimed at casual users rather than those requiring performance my 14x on the other hand has a much more powerful Intel i7 13700h processor taking a look at geekbench which tests a variety of common performance tasks the Zenbook 14 is just not a strong performer for a laptop in 2023 it performs worse than the HP dragonfly with a similar processor it has particularly poor performance in single core on the default standard fan profile we thought that this data point was a mistake but we retested several times and got the same result the 14x on the other hand is a very good performer it outperforms the Dell XPS 15 with the same processor and when on performance mode is on par with a base model MacBook Pro 14 with M2 switching to cinebench which tests how the laptop performs Under full load the Zenbook 14 continues to perform poorly in single core in multi-core like usual for this Benchmark the AMD ryzen processor shines that being said it's still behind the performance of the HP dragonfly with a similar processor the Zenbook 14x in this Benchmark is an absolute monster it completely dominates outperforming every other laptop to test thermal performance of the laptop we ran cinebench on a loop for 10 minutes the performance drop for both laptops was substantial that's when in the default standard fan mode it was less in the performance mode this indicates that the laptop's cooling solutions are just not capable of keeping the processors inside cool for long and that performance must be throttled this is where the MacBooks shine their M2 processors are far more efficient than those from Intel or AMD this is confirmed in the power draw graph both these laptops draw far more power than the max this again reinforces the poorer efficiency of Intel and AMD they need to draw so much power for the performance offered and it generates a lot more heat which is why you see the average power draws are substantially lower the laptop must reduce power to keep the processor cool FYI the CPU core temperatures are actually decent when it comes to temperatures you'd actually feel for light use like browsing the web and working on office documents the Zenbook 14 remained very cool to the touch the 14x though gets a little warm it is noticeable if like me you're sensitive to that sort of thing but I would say it's bearable when it comes to the fan noise under light use the Zenbook 14 was not great if you're in a quiet room the fans are frequently audible not loud but you can hear them this nbook 14x on the other hand was very quiet for this use case however when you do something that requires a bit of performance like installing an application you do hear some fan noise and occasionally it is high pitched so it's noticeable but the fans quickly return to quiet when the task is done by the way both laptops do have a quiet mode called whisper the power fed to the processor is dropped here and so is performance the Zenbook 14 on this mode was quieter but you could still hear the fans occasionally in a quiet room so not ideal the 14x though was dead quiet on this mode and felt less warm to the touch for high performance tasks the Zenbook standard profile like I recommend the fan noise gets allowed for this use case but it's not out of line from competitors on battery there is a hit to the laptop's performance unfortunately in titulo: Dell XPS 15 Review (9530) for 2023
transcricao: all right this laptop gets so hot under load I literally tried an experiment to see if I could cook my breakfast on it think I'm joking I am not but let's step back a moment and talk about this new XPS 15 for 2023 if you aren't familiar with the XPS 15 it's a premium laptop that targets content creators and those looking for performance on the go that being said it's not at the performance level that you would expect from a high-end gaming laptop something like an Alienware this year's model is basically the same laptop that Dell released 4 years ago with updated CPU and GPU options for 2023 Intel's 13th gen H series and nvidia's 4,000 series and that's the fundamental problem you're grabbing a laptop chassis that is well known to not be the best at cooling high performance components and then putting even higher performing components that run even hotter inside and in the case of this xps15 the issue isn't just inadequate cooling restricting the performance it's also the heat you feel while using the laptop even for casual tasks this laptop feels warm to the touch and the moment you start doing anything that requires performance it feels hot now a laptop this size with powerful components feeling warm at certain places that's not unusual but what makes this one so much worse than others is where it feels warm the hotpots are exactly where your fingers touch the keyboard the most it's around the palmrest and the W and I keys so it's super noticeable and this by the way was the reason I haven't recommended this laptop in the past even though there is a ton to love about it it's compact with lots of performance the keyboard is outrageously comfortable the trackpad is awesome and very accurate and the screen options are stunning it's even upgradeable where you can replace the RAM and storage yourself and this is all packaged in a premium feeling chassis so let's take a look and see how this new CPU and GPU perform in this chassis from 4 years ago starting with geekbench which test a variety of common CPU performance tasks it is beaten handily by the MacBook Pros with Apple's 12 core M2 processors in fact it's also beaten in multi-core performance by Dell's own XPS 17 from last year with Intel's 12g processor in fact comparing generation to generation this laptop is only 5% faster than last year's XPS 15 in single core and 8% in multi-core FYI here are my results from the newer geekbench 6 I'll probably switch over to it fully in a couple of months that's because some laptops that I wanted to compare this laptop too I no longer have and have only saved geekbench 5 scores switching to C bench which tests how this laptop performs Under full load compared to the xmg neo6 with the same CPU you can see how poorly this laptop performs in fact it performs around the same in multi-core as last year's XPS 15 and worse in single core to try to work work out what's going on here and why it performs so poorly I ran cinebench on a loop for 10 minutes basically a torture test to see how the laptop performs thermally there was a bit of a drop in performance now widening that Gap to the xmg neo6 which as I said has the same CPU you can see that this laptop doesn't come close to reaching the full potential of this processor the moment I took a look at CPU temperatures the reason became clear this laptop's processor hits a whopping 106 ° C I didn't think that was possible I thought a laptop CPU was forced to throttle its performance when temperatures hit 100° the most I've recorded before is 102 which I think is just an anomaly as the CPU switched to start throttling performance I even called up other laptop reviewers to ask what the max temperatures that ever recorded the highest number I heard was 105° so I think that this laptop now holds the crown of the hottest process are recorded and that isn't good but it does explain why we aren't getting any more performance out of the laptop CPU it's thermally constrained and it isn't just the internals that are hot as I said before keyboard temperatures when running performance tasks sore it to 49° C and fan noise during performance tasks was very loud and remember how I pointed out that the xmg neo6 with the same CPU perform much better it ran substantially cooler for the same fan noise is look if Dell are going to create a thin laptop transcricao: alright the MacBook Air with a 15 inch display was just announced and I think it's a very important product to talk about you see it plugs a massive hole in Apple's lineup finally we have a large screen Mac laptop for those who don't need a lot of performance people who are just using their laptop for web browsing office work and that sort of thing since it's basically a MacBook Air M2 the 13-inch with a larger screen and a bigger battery I feel pretty confident in sharing my early stage thoughts on it and FYI I'm trying to get this video out fast to you so apologies if production value is less than on our normal videos and by the way Apple also announced an augmented reality headset known as The Vision Pro rather than Jam my thoughts on that into this video I'm going to make a dedicated one on that later so make sure you're subscribed with the notification Bell on so you don't miss it back to the MacBook Air 15. let me share a personal story with you I mentioned my mother in almost every video well I wanted to get her a new laptop she just needs something for casual use responding to emails watching Netflix and writing office documents she really wants a large screen as her eyesight just isn't the best these days and sometimes she needs a bit of support and since I live in the USA and she's in Australia I can't provide that so I wanted to buy her a laptop where if she does need support there is excellent support available no laptop brand obviously the level of support that Apple does you can take the laptop into any store worldwide for help and even purchase Apple's excellent extended warranty so I knew I wanted to get her a Mac but the issue was the only large screen Mac available was a MacBook Pro 16. that laptop was heavy for her and it's too expensive as it has performers that she just doesn't need this MacBook Air 15 was available it would have been perfect for her and what I would have bought so let's now go beyond Apple's hype annoying amounts of hype to be honest and talk about what we really have here the MacBook Air 15 has the same 8 core CPU and 10 core GPU as the MacBook Air 13 with M2 the other end config that is based on the 35 watt charger being the same as the MacBook Air 13s my guide is there will be no increase in power delivery to the processor so we should have the same performance as the MacBook Air 13 with M2 in geekbench which tests a variety of common performance tasks it's around the same as the Intel 1360p processor in single core and a bit worse in multi-core and in cinebench which tests the processor's performance when maxed out it's worse in both single and multi-core in fact it's actually worse than Intel's low wattage 13th gen u-series processors its poor performance in cinebench by the way is affected by it being a fanless laptop a fanless laptop does have benefits in that the laptop is of course silent but it also has negatives when running anything that requires performance for any duration of time the performance of the processor will start to drop as the only way to keep it from overheating is to reduce the power fed to it secondly the laptop's metal chassis will gradually become warmer to the touch the laptop itself becomes one giant heatsink spreading the heat around to dissipate it by the way due to the MacBook Air 15's larger size I don't think it will get as warm when running performance tasks as the 13. and even though Apple's M2 chips do have excellent integrated graphics and you can do video editing on it I do not think people looking for performance should really buy this laptop they should continue to purchase the MacBook Pro 14 or 16 which have more robust cooling solutions and more powerful components next one of the good things about a larger laptop is you can fit a bigger battery in it the MacBook Air 15 now has a larger 67 watt hour battery compared to the 53 watt hour of the 13 inch but remember the MacBook Air 15 has to power a larger display that being said the MacBook Air 13 Within M2 already has incredible battery life during my battery life test where I lowered the screen's brightness to 200 nits then ran a Netflix video on repeat over Wi-Fi for 4 hours I recorded 68 battery remaining so around 12 hours of battery life for that use case the MacBook Air 15 which my guard tells me will exceed that it should be excellent when it comes to weight we are looking at 3.3 pounds which I think is excellent for a 15.3 inch screen size very light and portable and it will be a joy to carry around compared to other large green laptops in comparison Dell's premium XPS 15 weighs in at a much heavier 4.2 pounds compared to smaller screen 14-inch laptops the ThinkPad X1 Carbon is 2.5 pounds the yoga 9i is 3.1 and Apple's own MacBook Pro 14 is 3.5 so compared to the MacBook Pro 14 you are losing performance but getting on screen space and portability you no doubt once again have Apple's excellent speakers and their fantastic webcam but the notch in the display is still massive there are no additional ports and all the charging capable ports are on the left side so you will have to run a cable around the back if your power outlet is on the right side this can get in your way lastly you still have Wi-Fi 6 and not 6E or even the newer Wi-Fi 7. pricing on the surface seems good it starts at 1 300 for the base model but beware though this is for a very low end configuration with 8 gig of RAM and a 256 gig SSD also Apple's 256 gig ssds are notorious for being slower than their 5 12 gig drives it wouldn't surprise me if this issue carries across the new Macbook Air 15 if you spec it up to 16 gig of RAM and a more relevant 512 gig SSD you are already at 1 700 US dollars so this laptop is only well priced for users who have very basic needs which ties into my prediction for the MacBook Air 15. for users who want a large screen device and do not require performance this laptop is great and very competitively priced for what you get I think it will be an excellent choice for people just logging onto their work computer from home browsing the internet working on office documents or studying something that doesn't require a high performance laptop I think it'll be the best all-round device out there for you at that price range but it doesn't mean it eradicates Windows laptops from existence as Apple would have you think you can purchase lenovo's excellent yoga 9i on a regular sale for one thousand one hundred fifty dollars that laptop has a touchscreen is a two in one performs better for CPU tasks it feels cooler to the touch while using it and it comes with more memory and storage the MacBook Air 15 on the other hand performs better for GPU tasks has a larger screen a better trackpad much better battery life no fan noise better speakers and a better webcam oh and I do like that they have lowered the price on the entry model MacBook Air 13 with M2 by a hundred dollars that laptop is a great buy for the same type of user who should buy the 15 but who want more portability or who just don't need a larger screen props to Apple for that assets rare for a company to drop the price of anything in today's day and age for those looking to run performance applications on a Mac you should continue to purchase the MacBook Pro 14 or 16 as I said well those are my quick early stage thoughts on the new Macbook Air 15. I hope it helps you decide whether you should order one or get something else instead I did order one myself so I will do an updated video when it arrives I'm interested to know if you think early prediction videos like this one are helpful if you did let me know with a comment below anyway make sure to get subscribed and smash that like button not only does it show your appreciation for the effort gone into making these videos but as I always say it makes my mother very proud till next time go do something awesome with your day and I will catch you later

they need to be powerful enough to do what you need sounds simple right well most laptops fail miserably at one or more of these the LG gam 16 is for the most part a rare exception what makes it even more magical is how lightweight it is for what you get it weighs 1.2 kg which is around 2.7 lb for a laptop with a large 16-in screen that is light very light just to put that in perspective my Delux PS 13 plus which has a substantially smaller screen ways around the same this makes this device one of the most portable large screen laptops I've ever used but all is not perfect as you're about to see which has left me feeling that there is a set of users who are absolutely going to love this laptop and should buy it and others who should probably pass on it and get something else by the way best I've used on any laptop I feel this one is equivalent good travel with a satisfying click it is also backlit and has a number pad the trackpad is good enough for the most part tracking feels natural and I found it accurate in some obscure movements like when trying to repeatedly scroll down a page for filming this b-roll the cursor would occasionally jump to a different location or large 16-in panel with impressive color accuracy and enough brightness the panel is matte non-touch which means you won't see any Reflections it has the desirable 16x 10 aspect ratio for seeing a little more content for apps that go down the page and it has a resolution of 2560 x600 pixels which results in content looking crisp enough on screen at 188 pixels per inch in comparison a standard 13.3in laptop with a full HD 1920x 1080 panel would look slightly less crisp at 166 pixels per inch however this panel is not as sharp as the MacBook Pro 16s which hits 254 pixels per inch this all sounds good but I do want to call something important out the amount of content you can comfortably see on screen without needing to squint is a result of many factors the screen's brightness size and pixel density I how sharp things look on screen although this panel is physically large it isn't the brightest and it doesn't have the best pixel density because of this I couldn't run the laptop at 125% Windows scaling which is what I would need to do to see a lot of content on screen I found I was squinting when doing that I had to run the laptop on the default 150% Windows scaling where everything looked very large on screen and I didn't see enough content to Warrant such a large laptop on my you can see the substantial difference in the number of rows of excel I was able to see at these two scaling settings this is the first laptop I felt compelled to run a custom scaling setting on so I could use a percentage in between these two even Windows warns you against doing this as some applications may not scale correctly moral of the story I feel this panel needs to be brighter so you can make the most of its large screen size otherwise why bother I can see this much content comfortably on a smaller more portable 14-in laptop Port situation is good with two USBC ports that both support charging and our Thunderbolt two usba ports for backwards compatibility which are both the fast 10 GB variety an HDMI 2.0 port a headphone mic combo Jack and a Micro SD card reader my only knit is that both charging capable ports are on the left side so if your outlet is on the right you will need to run the charging cable around the back sound is okay it gets loud enough which is good but the speakers don't have the power nor the quality of a MacBooks sound quality is a little muddy and there isn't an immersive Sound Stage which is a Pity as this is a large laptop and you have the space to place speakers to create such an effect here's how the webcam looks and sounds in excellent lighting conditions it's a bit disappointing Windows hello facial recognition worked well and got me logged in fast let's talk performance for my performance test I tried both the normal and high fan speed settings which can be configured in the LG smart assistant app I used Windows balance performance mode with a normal fan setting and high performance mode with a high fan setting as you can see from gig bench which tests a variety of common short running tasks this laptop substantially underperforms the D xps13 with the same CPU both in single and multi-core that being said it did still perform better than my budget 6inch laptop pick the idad 5 Pro 16 with its ryzen 6 core CPU switching to cinebench which tests the laptop's processor went under full load things get worse it now significantly underperforms the dell and even underperforms the six core Rising processor I mentioned earlier in multi-core when I ran cinebench on a loop for 10 minutes for a torture test performance dropped further you can see that the amount of power fed to the processor dropped significantly during this test and so did the gigahertz that the processor runs at this is likely because the laptop can't effectively cool the Intel P series processor inside funnily enough when we look at the actual CPU core temperatures during this test you can see that LG do not allow the processor to hit 100° C like others do if LG did we would likely see more performance that being said if you want a laptop that doesn't run the processor at the max 100° C this may be the one when it comes to the temperatures you'd feel when using the laptop during performance tasks it's very competitive on balance mode with the normal fan profile it doesn't feel hot in performance mode though it can feel warm on the underside fan noise is another story on the normal fan mode you will hear the fan in a quiet room on half it becomes very noticeable more akin to a gaming laptop moral of the story do not buy this laptop if you plan to do anything intensive so let's talk about how the laptop performs in casual use like browsing the web working on office documents Etc if you run the laptop on normal fan speed as mentioned you will hear fans going in a quiet room it's not high pitched but you constantly will hear the word I then tried running the laptop on the no noise mode which was silent to my ears but unfortunately the laptop's performance perance was heavily throttled to achieve this I measured the CPU being throttled down to a completely unusable 400 MHz everything quickly became extremely laggy on that setting in my mind that setting should not even be offered on this laptop I ended up running it on the low calling mode when in a silent room that is in this mode the fans were still a titulo: Aero 14 Review: Powerful and Light! - But at a cost...
transcricao: gigabytes Aero series of laptops will always hold a special place in my heart the Aero 15 from back in 2019 was one of the laptops that helped me launch this Channel at that time I was on a mission to find a high-powered premium and portable laptop that's because my own use case consisted of some of the toughest things you could do on a laptop I was editing 4K videos programming and gaming and I needed to do all that while on the go the aerobrand it seemed like it was the perfect fit for my use case however it ended up falling a little short and about a hundred laptops later I'm still searching for the perfect one well today we have gigabytes new Aero 14 for 2023 which I hoped would finally deliver on that promise a high-powered portable and premium laptop I mean come on you've got an extremely powerful i7 13700h inside paired with a 45 watt Nvidia RTX 4050 and a gorgeous OLED display all in a very small and lightweight package at 3.3 pounds what could go wrong as you know I value your time so here's the skinny the Aero 14 does deliver on its promise of a lot of performance in a small lightweight package but it is a challenge to actually use for lightweight use like browsing the web you definitely hear disturbing fan noise and the chassis gets very warm to the touch the speakers and webcam are woeful and the ports on offer are lacking for this type of laptop alright let's dive into this in a little more detail starting with performance in geekbench which tests a variety of common performance tasks this laptop did extremely well when it compares to other powerful portable laptops the only one to beat it was the higher end MacBook Pro 14 with the 12 core M2 Pro CPU in cinebench which tests how the processor performs when Under full load again it performed exceptionally well only beef now by the Asus G14 in multi-core and that laptop uses an AMD ryzen Zen 4 processor and those processors are well known to do very well in this use case switching to Graphics this is the first RTX 4050 laptop that I've tested and it did not disappoint the Aero 14 is massively faster than my 3050 TI equipped Acer Swift on this laptop you will be able to get a taste of AAA gaming as well as do some 4K video editing that being said it doesn't compete with the RTX 4060 and 4070s available in larger laptops nor Apple's M2 processors for video editing moral of the story the Aero 14 is an incredible performer for its size particularly in CPU tasks where the fact that it is keeping Pace with and sometimes beating laptops that are physically much larger than it is very impressive I want to show you just how small the Aero 14 is the Alienware x14 has a much larger footprint than the Aero the Asus G14 is a good amount thicker heck even the MacBook Pro 14 feels a little larger alright the next thing I love about this laptop is the display it is stunning bright color accurate and crisp with its high resolution these factors combined to allow me to see a decent amount of content on screen without needing to squint at 175 window scaling which is why what I felt comfortable using I could see 38 rows of excel which is competitive for a premium 14-inch laptop the laptop also has a fast 90 Hertz refresh rate so movement on screen looks smoother also although PW and flickering is used to lower the brightness I felt that it was minimal and I really didn't have an issue with the implementation of it in this laptop the keyboard is also quite comfortable to type on the keys do feel a little low travel but they're soft feel and responsiveness kind of make up for that so that's quite a lot of positives but here's where using the laptop starts to be a struggle firstly the fan noise on this laptop specifically for light tasks is obnoxious it is some of the most disturbing I've heard for example I wrote this review with a fan mode set to Eco which is the laptop's quiet mode sitting in a silent room I could almost always hear the fans going and all I was doing is writing a script on Microsoft Word this is definitely not an intensive task and a modern laptop should be dead solid for this what was worse is the moment I did anything requiring an ounce of performance like opening up a Chrome tab the fans would all of a sudden spin up faster and be very audible it just gets worse though it wasn't just how loud the fans were that was disturbing it was that they kept spinning up and down which makes them even more noticeable this by the way has been an issue since my aero 15 which I bought four years ago gigabyte really need to improve their fan control algorithm particularly when the laptop is doing light tasks in performance tasks the laptop was very loud as well and by the way under no circumstance would I ever recommend running this laptop on turbo mode the fans on that mode are insanely loud now if you thought having the fans running a lot would keep the laptop feeling comfortably cool to the touch you'd be dead wrong just writing this review with nothing else running on the laptop the laptop's Palm rest felt noticeably warm to the touch I mean check out the difference in surface temperatures between this laptop and my MacBook Pro 14 for the identical task the Aero 14 is 7 to 8 degrees Celsius warmer which is definitely noticeable I found myself of regularly typing with my hands lifted slightly above the Palm rest to avoid the Heat and remember I'm talking about just writing a document on Microsoft Word here good luck doing something intensive on this laptop without using an external keyboard look you don't have to be a rocket scientist to know the problem here the laptop has a loud fan noise and feels hot because the components inside are way too powerful for this laptop's cooling solution if you've watched my channel recently I've been on a mission to test every 14 inch laptop so I'm a bit of an expert in this and I've witnessed many laptops this size struggle to call Intel's 13th gen P series processor which isn't less powerful than the h-series in this laptop I found Intel's lower wattage u-series processors more suitable for a laptop this size well in this laptop gigabyte have put in a high-powered h-series processor that processor really needs to be matched with a laptop that has a large chassis with very robust cooling solution like xmg's neo16 what makes this situation worse is they've also put in pretty powerful dedicated graphics which also needs to be called the only 14-inch laptop I've tested that can come close to handling similarly powerful components is the Asus G14 and that has a thicker chassis and is using an AMD ryzen processor alright the trackpad on the surface the trackpad is actually pretty good and tracking feels accurate but it is mechanical and when you click you lose a bit of accuracy particularly in the bottom corners for tasks that involve precise clicks like video editing or gaming which this laptop is meant to be designed to do you'd really want to use an external Mouse next the ports to demonstrate this issue let's take one of the main use cases that this laptop is marketed at content creating almost all cameras that creators use use use use full-size SD cards to transfer files the first problem is that this laptop has no full sized SD card reader only a micro one so creators are forced to either plug in an SD card reader into one of the USBC ports or plug the camera directly into one and that's where the second problem reads its head the only way to charge this laptop is with the single USBC port on the left side so anything that you want to connect via USBC has to be done on the right side since the ports are halfway down the laptop these cables now get in the way of using a mouse on either side which as I just said is really necessary on this laptop as you can see this is just not a well thought out design for one of the laptop's main intended use cases next the speakers they are atrocious there is negative bass here and at high volumes they just sound distorted I think these are good enough to use for vocals say a conference call but you wouldn't want to listen to music on them or watch a movie on this laptop fourth there are several unreliable things about the laptop minor ones though for example gigabytes Control Center Software where you go to change the fan settings and performance modes on occasion it just didn't open and sometimes driver updates were insanely slow next on occasion when I close the lid the laptop wouldn't go to sleep and I could just still hear the fans going next there are some miscellaneous things that I don't like the ram is soldered and not upgradable and the webcam sucks the webcam is n't the reason the audio is this processed happy running extends of noise cancellation to hide the fan noise lastly pricing this laptop is expensive at the time I wrote this review my unit was going for 1 650 it's a lot it's more than the Asus G14 and it's getting real close to the price of a MacBook Pro 14 with M2 which leads me to my conclusion yes if you want a ton of power in a Windows laptop that is super small and light this laptop will give it to you but there are serious sacrifices that you will be making look when I did use this laptop in a room with a lot of background noise other than the warm feeling keyboard deck I enjoyed it but the moment you start using the webcam or playing music things start to go downhill for the kind of user that I think would be interested in this laptop the Asus G14 which I also have is definitely worth considering it has far less disturbing fan noise particularly for casual use I'm referring to the 2023 version by the way which is much better in this department than the older 2022 one it also has far more powerful Graphics options and it's it's a bit cheaper in comparison the Aero 14 is slightly smaller has a more Vivid display and doesn't feel as hot at the touch for casual use yes even though I said this laptop feels warm to the touch for this use case the G14 is worse then if you're just looking at doing content creation on the go the MacBook Pro 14 crushes both of them it has far less heat and fan noise better battery life much better speakers and a better webcam and trackpad where you won't need an external Mouse and if you just want a good Windows laptop to consume content on or do office work on the Lenovo Yoga 9i or the HP Specter 13.5 are better choices I'll put links to all the laptops that I recommend down in the description below it's a shame as this laptop comes so close to being awesome hopefully gigabyte fixes the fan situation when the laptop is doing light tasks and in future puts in better speakers a better webcam and more titulo: Framework 13 (2023): Is it worth the hype?
transcricao: all right Tech family with me is one of the new framework laptops for 2023. if you haven't heard about framework they are a new company that burst onto the scene about two years ago their unique focus is on delivering a fully upgradable and repairable laptop which is exactly what we want this takes a lot of stress out of the buying process as you no longer have to decide up front what configuration you should get you can relax knowing you can upgrade it later on this also increases the longevity of the laptop and is of course better for the environment so let me quickly update you on what they've been doing over the last two years the biggest news is that they have updated their framework 13.5 with Intel's latest 13th gen and AMD ryzen zen4 processors I have one of them here today which I'm going to put through the paces and tell you all about they also have an upcoming larger 16 inch version which has upgradable graphics and a cool swappable keyboard design that allows you to switch between a centered keyboard or one with a number pad all laptops can be purchased as a full laptop or if like me you have an older framework you can just purchase the upgrade kit which is substantially cheaper than buying a completely new laptop so that's what I went with with the 13th gen i7 1360p motherboard upgrade by the way I would have chosen the ryzen Zen 4 version but it wasn't shipping till Q3 of this year I also have the new larger capacity battery it's a 61 watt hour up from 57 and it is the same physical size as the older one according to framework its capacity increase due to improvements in the lithium-ion chemistry I also have the new hinge which Promises to Keep the screen stable while making it easier to open with one hand which is welcome I did struggle to open the older one with one hand there is a new matte display option this will make the screen easier to read in bright lighting conditions that would have otherwise caused a lot of Reflections other than that it's the same panel same resolution colors and brightness I also have the new louder speakers and the new HDMI DisplayPort cards that will allow the laptop to stay in a low power state for better battery life while while you have them in the laptop framework has also released a bunch of other upgrades over the last two years such as a 2.5 gigabit Ethernet card and there is a Cooler Master case coming this case is super cool excuse the pun it will convert your framework motherboard into a small desktop again further increasing the longevity and reuse of these parts the upgrading process was as easy as it could be instructions were well laid out and the care that the framework team has put into designing the laptop to be easy to upgrade was evident for example the screws to open the back of the laptop all stay in place so you don't lose them when the cover is off the whole thing only uses one type of T5 screw bit there are no annoying clips that make it very hard to get the back off the laptop also it was cute that the team put their names and a message that the laptop was made with love inside and if you happen to want a job with them they put how to apply in there too as an experienced person in upgrading laptops it took me around 45 minutes to replace the motherboard the speakers and the battery which is pretty embarrassing I had two hiccups though there was one connector that I almost broke because I just looked at the pictures and didn't read the instructions don't do what I did read the instructions secondly I spent a lot of time trying to work out why I had an extra screw I thought there was something that I didn't screw in properly so I kept rereading the instructions I finally realized that the new motherboard came with a screw already screwed into the spot that keeps the SSD in place so that is why I had one extra after the upgrade I had to go through the BitLocker key entry if you don't want to have to do that turn off BitLocker before you upgrade the device BitLocker by the way it's Microsoft's disk level encryption just make sure you turn it back on after the upgrade if you want to ensure that people can't copy your files if your laptop is stolen once the upgrade was complete I ran framework software to update the laptop's drivers it was a very smooth process and after this everything seemed to work perfectly I did not have to reinstall Windows not update anything else loss when I say seemed as I mentioned I left BitLocker on before upgrading the device every time I restarted the laptop it would ask me to re-enter my key which was super annoying after I turned BitLocker off had it completely unencrypt the drive then restarted the laptop and turned it back on encrypting the drive everything was fine alright upgrade complete was it worth it hell yes the performance difference was immediately apparent with all drivers and software up to date and running in best performance mode in geekbench 6 single core was up 25 and multi-core a whopping 59 geekbench 6 by the way tests a variety of common performance tasks in cinebench which tests how the laptop performs Under full load single core was up 30 and multi-core literally 119 which is more than twice as fast wow if you are wondering what's happening behind the scene my older 11th gen version of the laptop Drew 50 watts of power at Max this new version draws 60 that being said the older version averaged around 28 watts of power over a 10 minute torture test that is Running Center bench on a loop the new version Drew 31 Watts clock speeds hit the advertised 5 gigahertz but then averaged at 2.4 and CPU temperatures hit the max of 100 degrees so you can really see the efficiency that's on display of Intel's 13th gen over the 11th under performance tasks the keyboard deck felt very comfortable at a Max of 42 degrees Celsius that Max by the way was around the top of the keyboard deck which you rarely use so good result there the underside though was hot I wouldn't want to run any performance tasks on this laptop if it was sitting on my lap when it comes to the speaker upgrade I definitely noticed an improvement the speakers were louder and clearer for the music tracks I measured I would say somewhere around 5 to 10 decibels the new speakers also had a better Sound Stage that being said they absolutely do not come close to the speakers in my MacBook Pro 14. these speakers lack the fullness of those there is literally no base on these at all so for the most part all looks good with the framework laptop right well not exactly the laptops fans are loud really really loud I measured 52 decibels when the laptop was under load on both my older Intel 11th gen version and the newly upgraded 13th gen 1. this is Extremely Loud definitely gaming laptop territory what's worse is it only takes a small performance task and the fan spin up to that loud volume for example Dropbox is currently doing a sync in the background and you can see that the fans are loud installing a program will also do this I'm not surprised this is the case as this laptop only has one fan most laptops with a processor this powerful would have too this means this single fan has to work harder to call the processor I checked Frameworks community and Reddit and others have absolutely reported this now I did try all the performance modes available balanced and best performance they both had the same issue with the fan fans quickly hitting 52 decibels when any performance task was run best power efficiency mode was much quieter though at 42 decibels still not silent and a little audible in a quiet room but better that being said the trade-off is a substantial drop in performance as the processor is now capped at 30 Watts I mean look at my geekbench scores on screen 62 of single core and 75 of multi-core my two cents framework should be offering these with lower powered and cheaper u-series processors you are paying for performance that you likely can't use due to excessive fan noise maybe offer just one skew with a P-Series processor for those who just don't care about the fan noise look we all hope the AMD ryzen's N4 version is more frugal with power and therefore doesn't run as hot for similar tasks but with this single fan design I think it may be wishful thinking you just can't beat physics the next issue is battery life for the test I lowered the screen's brightness to 200 nits then I ran the same Netflix movie on repeat over Wi-Fi for 4 hours at the end of the test it older 11th gen version with a smaller battery had 43 remaining and the newer 13th gen 1 with a larger battery 46 this indicates around seven hours of battery life for this use case look I'm disappointed here and by the way I spent a ton of time checking that there weren't Rogue programs running in the background I restarted the laptop and I ran the test multiple times same results this doesn't surprise me though as in practice I just haven't found Intel's 13th gen and 12th gen with those efficiency cores have really resulted in that much extra battery life and one more gripe albeit a minor one the new Intel 13th gen motherboard only supports ddr4 RAM and not the newer faster ddr5 this does make the new motherboards backwards compatible though with your old Ram as ddr5 modules do not use the same socket as ddr4 alright let's wrap framework are doing a lot of things right and I'm a big supporter that being said I have to call it as it is I think the main type of person who should buy this laptop is someone who is using it in a very loud environment that's because of the fan noise for example you are a software developer working in an open plan office or a loud co-working space for someone like you this laptop is a fantastic choice and the other type of user that I can see enjoying this laptop is someone doing very lightweight tasks who is happy to run the laptop in best power efficiency mode and is a dedicated supporter of framework's Mission to allow you to upgrade your laptops which is a noble one that's because you'd have to choose this over other external laptops like the MacBook Air with M2 which has many benefits over this one such as being dead silent offering far more powerful Graphics capabilities and having much longer battery life well what do you think of Frameworks offering for 2023 will you be buying one and if not what else are you looking at let me know in the comments below if you like this video you know what to do show me by Smashing the like button and getting subscribed not only does it show your appreciation for the insane amount of effort that goes into making these but as I always say it makes my dearest mother very proud if you need help picking your next laptop make sure to check out our Discord server where vetted laptop advisors are standing by to help you out link below till next time go do something awesome with your day and I will catch you later

transcricao: all right Tech family this is a story of a laptop that could have been great great for so many people but due to hp's rather bizarre choices it is not instead what we have here is a laptop that is just above average and only really viable for certain people at a certain price point now don't get me wrong I personally enjoyed using this laptop I really did as I fit into the user segment where this laptop shines but that's what makes this review so frustrating it's a story of Lost opportunity this laptop could have been so much more so buckle up and let me show you who should buy this laptop and what price you should buy it for and FYI I am doing Orthodontics right now so if you see something weird on my teeth that's the explanation alright the dragonfly brand is something that HP has had out in the commercial space for some time they're kind of like a high-end laptop for business users if you've ever worked in a large corporation you'll know that many of them cheap out on the laptops that they buy their employees so hind in the business space is around say mid-range in the consumer space anyway recognizing that commercial and personal users are actually the same people HB is trying to launch this brand into the consumer space calling this laptop the HP dragonfly Pro but what you're about to see is that this laptop is neither Pro nor was there any reason to introduce another brand into the consumer space making their lineup more confusing let me first outline who I think this laptop is good for and the way I'm going to do this is through a process of elimination what we have here is a premium feeling 14 inch laptop that's somewhat portable it's actually quite heavy for a 14-inch laptop especially considering it does not have any powerful Graphics capabilities so straight away we can rule out anyone who needs a laptop for graphics intensive tasks yes the AMD integrated Graphics is better than Intel's but you really aren't going to want to buy this laptop if you want to do any AAA gaming or say video editing so what about CPU processing power for people who might need that say like software developers well initially it looks like this laptop performs well in hp's press material they position it as a competitor the Dells XPS 13 plus and Apple's MacBook Pro 14. in geekbench which has common performance tasks it performs similar in multi-core to the XPS 13 plus and the original M1 version of the MacBook Pro 14. and in single core it lags a bit in cinebench which tests how the processor performs Under full load it does very well in multi-core but lags a bit in single core compared to other processors from 2023 this isn't surprising as even though this is a 7000 series AMD processor for 2023 it's actually one of amd's misleadingly named ones as it is a Zen 3 processor that's the architecture that came out last year rather than the zen4 one from this year's architecture but but but the scores I just showed you are actually hugely misleading all you need to do is run the geekbench test a second time and performance drops a ton check out my two gig bench scores that I ran in succession on screen big drop I tried the same test on both my dragonfly Pro laptops I have two of them and on multiple different bias versions F10 f11 and F12 the performance drop is consistent no matter what I mean check out how inconsistent my performance results are on this laptop as I ran the benchmarks multiple times you can see it on screen this is insane I initially thought perhaps this is due to HP software which controls the performance profiles you can't set this laptop to a high performance mode like you would on other laptops instead HP switches it back to balance mode as they control the performance themselves as in they try to determine when you need high performance and when you don't but then I ran cinebench on a loop for 10 minutes and compared it to my performance results of a short single run a big drop again it appears that this laptop cannot sustain its performance for any duration of time the cooling solution it just isn't good enough given the max speeds that they allow the fans to run it and the temperatures they allowed the CPU to get to so given what I already said I wouldn't recommend this laptop to someone needing a lot of CPU performance switching to light users those who just use their laptop for casual tasks like browsing the web using office applications and things like that those tasks they just don't require a lot of CPU performance the laptop was extremely Snappy for those that being said all it took was to install a new application and the fans would kick in they weren't overly loud but they were high pitched like a soft Whistling noise this made the fan noise more noticeable in comparison to Dell's XPS 13 plus or the MacBook Pro 14 the ones HB Compares this laptop to this just doesn't happen on those let's now look at the rest of the laptop starting with the ports you've got three USBC ports all supporting charging and two of which are Thunderbolt 3. the issue here is that you have no variety of ports no usb-a no HDMI no SD card and what's really tough to swallow is you have no headphone jack I rarely use a headphone jack as I mainly use Bluetooth headphones but the admission of this it just kind of sucks for example I couldn't plug the laptops straight into my studio Mackie speakers which would have been nice the display is initially very pleasing to look at it gets plenty bright and has excellent contrast you will notice in my b-roll it is very glossy and reflective when actually using the laptop though that wasn't much of an issue now even though it has a large 14 inch screen you can't really take full advantage of it as the screen isn't that pixel dense the laptop is only available with a 1920x1200 resolution panel stretched across 14 inches that is only a pixel density of 161. a MacBook Pro 14 that is is significantly sharper at 254 pixels per inch this means that content isn't as crisp on screen and when I ran my test of how many rows of excel I was comfortably able to see without needing to squint titulo: Be More Productive with a Portable Monitor: LG gram +view
transcricao: all right Tech family I walked in the door to find our video editor editing with his laptop plugged into this portable external monitor the LG plus view we get a lot of products sent to us and it is super rare that we end up using them ourselves the ones we do are really the best of the best plus I personally am a big believer that external monitors increase productivity I used to live in a small one-bedroom apartment you would have seen it in my older videos in that apartment I had no desk and worked with the laptop on the dining room table at dinner or when we had gas over I'd have to first put away the laptop heck one of the reasons I started reviewing laptops on this channel was I couldn't get a desktop as I had nowhere to put it so I needed to find a great laptop the downsides of a laptop of course is having to work on a smaller screen I would have loved to have an external monitor like this one one that was quick to set up and pack down now LG sent me this monitor kind of like an add-on to be included in my review of the LG gram 16 but since this monitor is a leap above other portable external monitors I've used it deserves its own video first why we love it it's a large 16 inch panel with respectable brightness at 350 nits and excellent color reproduction it's very portable weighing in at just under one kilogram which includes the magnetic protective cover that doubles as a stand it's also convenient to use the display has two USBC connections located on either side all you do is plug in the USBC cable it comes with into your laptop and then control the brightness with the brightness rocker no external charging cable needed it is a highest resolution panel at 2560 by 1600 giving it a PPI of 189 pixels per inch so text on screen will look sharp enough for most people Chelsea you get a sense of where that lies a standard 13.3 inch laptop with a full HD 1920x1080 resolution screen would be a PPI of 166 so better than that but nowhere near sharp as a retina panel on a MacBook Pro which has a PPI of 254. it also supports up to a 75 Hertz refresh rate so movement on screen will look slightly smoother than on a regular 60hz panel the panel is matte which means you won't see Reflections on the display this also means you can get away with a slightly less bright panel like this one as you don't need High brightness to combat those reflections with that all said we found this monitor extremely useful in raising our overall productivity for example our video editor would have notes up on the external display while editing a video on the laptop's one I would have a spreadsheet up of test results on the external monitor while I wrote a script summarizing them on the laptop's one yes you can obviously divide up your laptop's display to do this but it is far easier to have a second one and of course you get more screen real estate here are a couple of other good use cases if you are traveling and want something to help you raise your productivity while away this is great for that if your laptop doesn't have a color accurate display and you want one rather than replacing the entire laptop you could buy this funnily enough I love lenovo's Legion series but the one criticism I have of them is that the color reproduction it isn't good enough for professional color work paired with the LG Grand plus view problem solved at a price of around 300 US dollars for these kind of use cases I think it's definitely worth considering heck as a bonus benefit if you wanted to gain above 60 hertz this monitor will at least let you get up to 75 without replacing your laptop I don't think that that one though is worth it in isolation but I thought I'd mention it so here's a couple of things to be aware of before you buy it firstly the monitor requires power and cannot be powered directly it draws power only from the cable that it is plugged into the laptop with therefore when using the monitor when the laptop is on battery it will reduce the battery life you get out of it second as the monitor is 2560 by 1600 map panel it is best paired with laptops with a similar panel like its sister laptop the LG gram 16. you can use it with other laptops of course but the experience of moving your eyes between the laptop screen and the external monitor may not feel as seamless for example if you're looking at a laptop's display that has a poorer color accuracy then you look across to this display it might be a little disjointing next the cover stand attaches via magnets and it works well when the monitor is in landscape mode the angle isn't adjustable though it also doesn't really work when the monitor is in portrait mode it would have been nice if LG added magnets so it could be used in portrait mode as well also I noticed the monitor wouldn't work when plugged into either my tiny Dell XPS 13 or Dell XPS 13 plus it worked on larger laptops I tried like my MacBook Pros LG gram Legions and Aero 15. my untested hypothesis is though smaller laptops don't provide enough power by the USB ports I did order a multimeter so I can test this in future next it would be nice if the monitor acted as a USB hub some laptops don't have a lot of ports and since this monitor has two it would be great if I could plug a USB device into it so one of my laptops isn't tied up driving the monitor that being said I was able to plug my phone into the monitor while it was plugged into a laptop and at least power does pass through and I was able to charge my phone like that finally this monitor for a portable one is large and as I said it is meant to be used in landscape mode if you are a coffee store entrepreneur you probably aren't going to fit a laptop with this monitor on a standard two-seater coffee store table so let's wrap we love the LG Grand plus view and honestly found it to be one of the most useful devices we've ever used to raise productivity it's the first time I feel 100 confident recommending one of these portable external monitors if you aren't able to add a regular external monitor to your setup for whatever reason the LG Grand plus view is absolutely worth considering well that's all for today folks if you like this video you know what to do smash that like button and get subscribed it shows your appreciation for the insane amount of work that goes into making these and as I always say it makes my mother very proud till next time go do something awesome with your day and I will catch you later
