titulo: HP Spectre x360: Premium Laptop for a Budget Price
transcricao: Tech family today I'm going to tell you what it's like to own and use the HP Specter 13.5 X360 for 2022 who should buy it how it compares to last year's model and other competitors that you may be considering because I've been using this laptop almost exclusively for the last couple of weeks and I personally bought and owned last year's model myself so I'm very familiar with this device but before I get into it do me a favor if at the end of this video you like what you watched make sure that you're subscribed to the channel and click the like button it shows your appreciation for the insane amount of effort that goes into making these plus as I always say it makes my mother very proud just a heads up on the naming of this laptop I've seen it called both the Specter X360 13.5 and the Specter X360 14. last year as I recall it was called the Specter 14 but it had a 13.5 inch screen in marketing material sent to me this year it is called the 13.5 but some of hb's own documentation still seems to be calling it the 14. it's the same device though anyway let's start with the things I love about this laptop and why I personally bought one last year this laptop has the most comfortable keyboard of any laptop that I have ever tested if you value a great typing experience you must try this keyboard secondly the OLED screen is a joy to look at it's very color accurate it's bright it's high resolution and the rare 3x2 aspect ratio will ensure you see a ton of information on screen specifically for applications that go down the page like word web browsers and software development Ides it's almost the perfect display with two exceptions to call out pwm flickering is used this turns the screen on and off very fast to control brightness I normally find this causes my eyes to get tired over time but I didn't have any issues in my use of this laptop and lastly it only has a 60hz refresh rate so movement on screen won't won't be as smooth as on a faster refresh rate display but all in all it's a display that your friends will be envious of if you have this device looks and feels premium one of my staff saw it and immediately exclaimed wow that is a nice looking laptop and it is that being said color is subjective I personally don't love this Nightfall black color but if I was to buy this laptop I would only purchase it with this color or the blue that's because the silver model likely has light colored keys with a light colored backlight which will make the keys very hard to make out in certain lighting conditions HP is notorious for doing this on their laptops with silver colored keys back on the sturdiness of the chassis the exterior edges of the laptop feel sturdy however when you press in the center of the lid you will notice some Flex there is also a little Flex on the keyboard deck but I didn't find that too distracting in real use for the screen size and the build quality this laptop is portable enough I love that HB includes a super tiny 60 5 watt USBC charger that helps with the total carry weight of this laptop here's how the webcam looks and sounds in excellent lighting conditions it's filming in 1440 and I think it looks pretty decent the laptop can be flipped around to use as a tablet and comes with a tilt pen that worked well although I'm not a graphic artist so I'm not sure how well it really works and for a premium laptop the pricing is excellent if you pick this laptop up on sale Best Buy for example tends to regularly put this laptop on sale for several hundred dollars off so as you can see there is a lot to love about this laptop but one of the main reasons I got this laptop info review was to see if the issue I had with last year's had been fixed I bought last year's model with my own money as my personal laptop for script writing and web browsing as I said I chose it because of what I just mentioned a great keyboard excellent screen and form factor but unfortunately the cooling solution couldn't handle the power hungry Intel i7 1165 G7 processor inside what would happen is in light use the fans would all of a sudden come on very loud to try to call the laptop this was extremely disturbing and I eventually sold the laptop because of this I was worried that this year HP would do something silly and again try to cram in a high-powered processor just like other manufacturers are done by putting Intel's P-Series processors inside their small thin laptops but to my little light HB has chosen to put a less power hungry u-series processor inside I can tell you just from using it it no longer has the issue of last year's model the fans do not come on blasting out of the blue that being said this is also still not a completely quiet laptop you will hear some fan noise in everyday use but it's more of a consistent low volume than a sudden jet engine so let's see how this Intel 12 gen i7u series processor performs I'm going to test both the default balance mode and performance mode configurable in the HP Command Center Software we will start with geekbench which has a variety of common short running tasks you can see that it performs much better than last year's Intel 11th gen model not even in the same league in terms of multi-core it's competitive it beat out the 6 core 12 thread ryzen 5 6600 HS in the IdeaPad 5 Pro 14 I recently tested switching to cinebench which tests the laptop when Under full load it again destroys the model from last year that being said as you can see the Intel 12th Gen u-series processor in this laptop and my X1 Carbon is not the strongest performing processor out there for a 14 inch laptop you should look elsewhere if you want the best performance but honestly a score of over 8 000 in cinebench it's not bad either looking at how the laptop maintains its performance over a 10 minute torture test you can see that when in best performance mode there is a drop but not by that much looking at the laptop's power draw during this test you can see that the default balance mode is quite Frugal in its power draw but under best performance mode the laptop initially draws 42 Watts but then drops averaging 29 watts of power over the 10 minute torture test this shows that the cooling solution in this laptop simply can't effectively call this processor by the way take a look at how efficient the MacBook Pro 14 with the M1 Pro chip is compared to this in Intel processor it performed better drawing less power here is the CPU temperature for the torture test no surprises it maxes at 100 degrees Celsius on best performance causing the laptop to drop power fed to the processor to try to cool it by the way I did not test graphics performance of this laptop extensively as the integrated graphics performance of these Intel chips is extremely subpar when compared to apple or AMD don't buy this laptop if you want a game or do video editing overall performance is a big step forward from last year and I'm happy enough with it I do think HP made the right choice as to which processor to put in the laptop well given how unavailable AMD ryzen 6000 new series processors seem to be however I will say this in everyday use although the laptop was fast enough it wasn't the snappiest Performing laptop that I've used the MacBook Pro 14 for example was noticeably faster let's now look at heat you'd feel while using the laptop and fan noise you hear when the laptop is under full load doing high performance tasks the keyboard deck feels warm and the underside feels hot you'll want to use the laptop on a desk for this fan noise was acceptable when on balance mode but became quite noticeable on best performance mode in everyday use like browsing the web using office applications Etc as I said you could always hear the fans going if you listen closely and over time the laptop would feel a little warm there cooler feeling quieter laptops out there for sure performance when on battery is quite decent there isn't much of a drop particularly when you run the laptop on best performance mode and to test battery life I set the screen's brightness as close to 200 nits as possible I then ran a movie from Netflix playing on a repeat over Wi-Fi for 4 hours at the end I recorded 57 remaining so you should be able to get around eight and a half hours of battery in a similar use case probably more if you lower the brightness further which is a pretty decent result so let me just quickly run you through several things that I don't love about this laptop that you must be aware of before buying it the trackpad is too slippery I found it hard to get comfortable with and yes I tried turning down the sensitivity by comparison it's less slippery and more comfortable to use than the trackpad I recently tested in the ThinkPad z13 this seems to be a trend for manufacturers of high-end PC laptops to put slippery trackpads in please stop the poor placement in this year's model is ridiculous the headphone mic combo Jack has been moved to the diagonal back edge of the laptop where the USBC Port is on the other side these ports are hard to plug cables into since you can't see them from where you would sit facing the laptop they are also easy to knock the USBC connections also don't seem to go fully in which is odd and unfortunately both charging capable ports are on the right side so you'll have to run a cable around the back if your outlet is on the other side the sound although loud is a bit muddy sounding it definitely does not compete with the speakers in Apple's MacBook Pros and saving the worst till last closing the lid of my Specter 13.5 does not cause the laptop to sleep it keeps running as if the laptop is open you can see my b-roll the keyboard backlight is still on when the laptop is closed this has caused my laptop to get very warm in my backpack and the laptop runs itself out of battery power this also happened on my model from last year and lastly this is one of those laptops that doesn't seem to sleep properly When I close the lid here's an example where I'm watching the office close the lid and you can hear it keep playing come on you can tell me Jim tell me anything this is completely unacceptable that being said I've searched the net and it does not seem that others are reporting this issue so perhaps I just happen to get two lemons only buy this laptop if you can return it if this occurs and if it does swap it to a different unit or a different laptop so let's wrap the Specter 13.5 X360 is one of the better laptops that I've reviewed this year specifically for those who are looking for a laptop for office work browsing the web or school for this use case you've got one of the best keyboards in a laptop a display others will be envious of it's lightweight given the size of the screen there's enough performance and the price is very good the main downsides are that you will hear a bit of fan noise while using it and if you get a unit like mine that won't sleep when you close the lid you will obviously need to return it that being said for the use case that suits this laptop if you can afford a MacBook Pro 14 and are okay with Mac OS I prefer you go that route it's a better laptop overall it's more powerful has better battery life better ports speakers Etc you will sacrifice a bit of portability compared to the Specter though as the MacBook is a little heavier and when it comes to comparing the MacBook Air with M2 to this laptop this laptop's keyboard is quite a bit better so it's a bit closer that being said I'd still recommend you get the MacBook Air with M2 over this but if you do want a PC laptop and you can find the Specter on one of those regular rotating sales that it is known to go on it is very competitive and I'd strongly consider it compared to the XPS 13 plus that laptop feels more premium and it's more portable due to its size but the Specter can be found at a better price and can be more useful due to its screen size and aspect ratio I'm also testing how it compares the new X1 Carbon right now so make sure you're subscribed with the notification Bell on as you'll be the first to hear my thoughts on that laptop well that's all for today folks if you need help choosing a laptop make sure to check out our Discord server where vetted laptop advisors are standing by to help you out till next time go do something awesome with your day and I will catch you later

titulo: iPhone 14 Pro Max Review: Why I Returned It
transcricao: Tech family today I'm going to share my experiences with the iPhone 14 pro Max an excellent device but one that I believe was completely overhyped on launch and that you should really think twice about before purchasing or default purchasing as many Apple buyers do if you're new here a little about me I'm completely unbiased when it comes to Tech I use the best device at the time for the job that I'm doing I'm currently a big fan of Apple's laptop range and have both their MacBook Pro 14 and 16 in ones but a couple of years ago when they had their Intel butterfly keyboard laptops I wasn't and these devices were all purchased by me independently of Apple there is a patreon link down below if you'd like to support the channel to help me do this but if you aren't able to financially help don't worry just take a moment to click the Subscribe button if you haven't already that alone shows your appreciation for the effort spent making these videos and as I always say it will make my mother very proud but let's turn back the clock I was in India walking down the streets of Bangalore and I tripped on the pavement and dropped my beloved Samsung S21 Ultra if you live or have been to Bangalore you'll know the sidewalks can be pretty rough anyway I dropped the ultra many times before and it had never been damaged but this time things were different there was a massive crack across the screen and the phone started to stop responding to my touch guys if you travel to a mobile dependent country and you don't bring any local currency like I didn't bring a second phone as a backup as finding your way around can be scary without one as luck would have it before I left I'd ordered the new iPhone 14 pro and pro Max to review on this channel I was looking forward to trying Apple's latest as I had been an Android User since my iPhone 7 plus back in 2016. anyway when I got home I eagerly unboxed my iPhone 14 pro Max and after several weeks of solid use here are my thoughts on the positives the screen is stunning it's so crisp and immersive I honestly found myself just walking across roads into oncoming traffic as I was distracted by the video I was watching the sound from the speakers is excellent noticeably better than my Samsung S21 Ultra and s22 plus and the device it just feels so solid and premium you feel just proud holding it and the phone it is fast loading and switching between apps was super quick scrolling insanely smooth definitely felt faster than on my Android phones and the camera as expected is excellent Straight Out of the Box the colors look natural and they don't look as saturated as they do on my Samsung phone's default camera app when it comes to Apple's ecosystem the iPhone fully unlocks it seeing calls pop on my MacBook Pro 14 and being able to choose whether to answer them there or on the phone own is super cool iMessage and FaceTime they really are great and so easy to use as they are so tightly integrated and the speed and security of face ID unlock is very welcome my Apple Powerbeats Pro earphones started working like they should have for the last two years I took them out of the case bam they were connected to the phone and working with my Android phones they would occasionally just not connect or disconnect so as you can see I think this is a mighty nice device but here's why I believe it's over hype and you should really give Android devices a look before you buy firstly with its solid construction comes white with my kickstand case which I believe is a must to make the most of this phone it weighed in at over 290 grams that's the same weight as an iPad Mini which has a much larger 8.3 inch display and because the weight the size ratio of this device is so high it definitely feels heavy to hold by the way I'll place a link to the case I recommend in the description below when you combine the weight with the fact that Apple continues to place the back button in the top left corner of the screen it means you frequently need both hands to operate this phone as the back button is one of the most frequently used functions on a phone Android devices have this button placed conveniently bottom right where your thumb is next connectivity is a disappointment you've still got the proprietary lightning Port which has a max transfer rate of USB 2's 480 megabits USB 2 was launched in April 2000. this device not having USBC is race on so many fronts pretty much all other high-end devices are now using USBC with faster charging and data transfer speeds why do I have to have a specific cable just to charge some of my Apple devices and I say some because many Apple devices have USBC in fact they were one of the first major companies to ditch usb-a and adopt only USBC on their 2016 MacBooks it's wasteful and bad for the environment that we have to use this stupid proprietary cable instead of being able to share the cables that our other devices use apple has this whole page on social responsibility and what they're doing for the environment forcing us to use this stupid cable negates it and when it comes to Wi-Fi the phone doesn't support the latest and faster Wi-Fi 6E which introduces the faster six gigahertz Band Wi-Fi 6E is rolling out in almost all routers being released this is Apple's most expensive phone and was launched in the second half of 2022 Wi-Fi 6A should be in here Samson had it in their premium devices from the beginning of this year so enjoy waiting around to get those large photos or video files that this phone is capable of taking off the phone and onto your computer next the advertisements you are literally paying top dollar for Apple to advertise to you the advertisements in Apple's App Store are so big and in your face more so than on Google's Android play store plus I'm constantly being berated and pushed into using Apple's apps like Siri I don't want to use Siri I already use Amazon's Alexa at home I don't need another virtual assistant and talking about Amazon with their Kindle Fire devices their devices are subsidized because they are using them as opportunities to advertise to you not here of course with Apple's iPhone next if you use a PC laptop or computer you can't use iMessage on the flip side that's not the case if you have an Android phone Google has a web version of their text messaging app that you can use titulo: Almost Perfect: ThinkPad Z13
transcricao: all right Tech family with me is lenovo's ThinkPad z13 a highly requested laptop on this channel why because on the surface it takes every box you could look for in a premium super portable laptop it's got a gorgeous edge to edge display a solid high quality chassis a comfortable ThinkPad keyboard and the most desirable processor available in a PC laptop right now an AMD ryzen 6000u series one from the outside this looks like the perfect premium portable laptop and it almost is except two things now I value your time so I'm not going to make you watch the video to find out the trackpad is really tough to get used to and the pricing starting at 2 000 US dollars is too high but since it's still a very good laptop here's my review by the way stating the obvious as this is a premium laptop my bar is higher than for laptops that cost a lot less screen is great I have the 1920x1200 model I was worried the display would seem noticeably more pixelated than the 4K plus display on my Dell XPS with a similar size screen it didn't there was enough pick pixels for the small size screen brightness peaked at over 400 nits which is great colors for on-screen content viewing were very good but for editing photos or films on this laptop the Adobe RGB and P3 coverage isn't as good as on a macbook's display the amount of content you can comfortably view on screen without needing to squint is determined by multiple factors including screen brightness pixel density and screen size when I ran my Excel test to see how much content I could see on screen without needing to squint this laptop showed the least out of its competitors I believe this is due to the lower pixel density and the slightly smaller 13.3 inch screen verse say the 13.4 inch of the XPS 13 plus and the 13.6 of the MacBook Air M2 if you purchase a z13 with a higher density 2880 by 1800 display you may find yourself able to see more content on screen the screen is 60 hertz and I detected no PW on flickering or annoying Reflections during my use also the touchscreen worked well and was a nice touch the keyboard was one of the stars of the show thinkpads used to be known as having the most comfortable keyboards of any laptop available but recent thinkpads I've tested unfortunately took a turn for the worse their keyboards fought noticeably low travel they weren't bad but not at the heights of thinkpads of old the good news is this keyboard is back to feeling very comfortable to use yes still a little low travel but it's definitely one of the more comfortable laptop keyboards around it has satisfying click as you press the key the downside is that it is loud if you are an intense touch hyper and you attend a lot of in-person meetings or classes other people in the room will likely hear you typing and be distracted a couple more notes on the keyboard I am glad to see that this is the first ThinkPad I've used that uses a traditional keyboard layout and doesn't have the function and control key swapped you could swap them back in lenovo's Vantage software of course but it annoyed me that they had such fundamental keys in different places yes I know ThinkPad lovers that it's a historical ThinkPad theme the trackpad I don't love in fact I believe it is the biggest downside of this laptop there are three reasons I don't like it first it's very slippery and hard to be accurate on even when I tried slowing down the cursor speed second if you use this laptop propped up on your lap either in bed or on a couch it has trouble registering your fingers movements if something like a blanket or article of clothing is touching the trackpad there were many times that I was using the laptop on the couch on a blanket and my finger gliding across the trackpad wasn't registered at all and third the trackpad has a physical line and dots in it that make gliding over this part of the trackpad feel disjointed and distracting what's happened is to support the iconic red trackpoint they have removed the physical buttons for it that used to sit above the trackpad and instead expanded the trackpad size this I like but they have marked a part of the trackpad with this physical line to separate the button area for the track point unfortunately this approach really screws up the trackpad experience I'd suggest leaving the red trackpoint and just going with a smooth trackpad surface Ifill will still know where to click the chassis looks like a stylish business laptop and when you touch it it feels very high quality the laptop is also light and portable I was surprised to find it didn't come with Lenovo super tiny 65 watt USBC charger that came with my ThinkPad Nano instead it came with a standard size one I'd suggest buying the Nanos one which I'll link below by the way I thought I wouldn't like the lip at the top of the screen housing the webcam but it made the laptop super easy to open with one hand which I liked ports are good enough on a super small laptop with a headphone mic combo Jack and two fast USB 4 ports that both support charging they are placed on either side of the laptop which means you won't have to run a power cable around the back if your outlet is on the other side of the laptop a good thing as the cable can get in the way sound from the speakers is good substantially louder than on my Dell XPS 13 plus which honestly is way too quiet but not as good as on a MacBook fingerprint reader and windows hello login both worked well and got me logged in fast here's how the z13's webcam looks and sounds in excellent lighting conditions honestly the colors look off you can see this should be white behind me I don't think it's Auto detecting the white balance correctly and for comparison here's what the webcam looks and sounds like on the MacBook Pro 14. for performance let's start with geekbench which tests a variety of common short running tasks it's substantially slower than the competition particularly in single core switching to cinebench which tests the laptop when it's under full CPU load it performs very well beating up both the Intel P-Series CPU in my Dell XPS 13 plus and the M2 MacBook Air this is not uncommon for AMD CPUs by the way they tend to perform best in sustained heavy workloads particularly as they run less hot than Intel CPUs and therefore don't have to be throttled as much to keep the CPU at a safe operating temperature that being said in this small chassis Lenovo struggles to keep this powerful AMD CPU cool when I ran cinebench R23 continuously for a 10 minute torture test you can see a large drop in performance you can see the power fed to the processor drops substantially during that time more so than on my Intel Dell XPS 13 plus please note the MacBook Air M2 doesn't have a fan at all so the reason it is dropping is because reducing the power fit to the processor is the only lever it has to keep that device cool CPU temperatures all peaked at 100 degrees or more in the case of my MacBook Air M2 by the way as you may have seen in these graphs I really didn't notice any performance difference from running the laptop in its Extreme Performance mode versus the default intelligent Cooling and yes all firmware drivers and software are the latest when it comes to heat you feel when the laptop is under full load the laptop feels very warm to the touch fan noise is loud but not quite as loud as competitors for everyday use though I found my Dell XPS 13 plus with Intel 12 gen P series faster than this laptop when I was logged into a work environment via Citrix while on a zoom call with about 10 browser tabs open I noticed a little lag on the z13 that I didn't notice on my Intel laptop that was when both laptops were running on their default performance mode by the way I also heard more fan noise on this laptop than on the XPS honestly my two cents this chassis can't adequate really cool this powerful ryzen 7 8 core processor if you are going to buy this laptop I'd lean towards buying one with the cheaper less powerful ryzen 5 6 core model it's likely better suited for this laptop by the way the integrated graphics performance of the ryzen 6000 u-series CPU is much better than Intel so if you're planning to game on your laptop and are choosing between an Intel or AMD without dedicated graphics get AMD when on battery performance does drop a bit less than on my Intel XPS 13 plus though for my battery life test I set all settings for the best possible battery performance then I lowered the screen brightness to around 200 nits I played a Netflix movie on repeat over Wi-Fi for 4 hours at the end of the test I recorded 66 battery remaining which is very good if we extrapolate out you should be able to hit close to 12 hours on the z13 with the display I have I did retest my XPS 13 plus at the same time and it had 49 remaining however my XPS does have the high resolution 4K display light which likely draws more power but on the flip side the z13 has a smaller battery at 51.5 watts versus the XPS is 55. this is a fantastic result for the z13 and really shows off the power efficiency of the AMD processor let's wrap talking about pricing this laptop is very expensive on Lenovo side it started over 2 000 US Dollars that's for the six Core ryzen 5 model by the way and for the ryzen 7 model but I have more than 2 500. I did find it a lot cheaper on B H's site for two thousand dollars for the model I have I'll place a link to that in the description below if you want to buy this laptop but overall I really think that this is a bit too expensive that's around 500 more than the XPS 13 plus and 300 or so more than the MacBook Air M2 upgraded with similar specs overall this is a very solid premium portable laptop and you'll most likely be happy if you buy it particularly if you're someone who mostly uses the laptop on a desk and or uses external mouse that way you'll avoid the trackpad issues that I had compared to the XPS 13 plus this laptop doesn't have the quirks that that one has such as non-physical function buttons this laptop speakers are better its Graphics are more powerful it has longer battery life and this laptop rarely feels warm to the touch the XPS on the other hand has acquired a keyboard better CPU performance in most tasks and less fan noise if they were priced the same I'd probably slightly lean you towards purchasing the z13 over the XPS the MacBook Air M2 has a larger screen it also has long battery life it has no fan noise at all and it looks sexier the z13 has a more comfortable keyboard and it can run Linux which by the way worked well if price the same I probably get the MacBook Air but that's the issue they aren't priced the same even at the best pricing I could find this laptop it needs to drop by several hundred dollars for me to consider it there just isn't enough here for me to definitively say go buy it over other premium portable laptops especially with its trackpad and on the trackpad note I personally use these laptops that I review as my daily driver and so glad that this review is over having to use this laptop for the last couple of weeks with its trackpad it was challenging well that's all for today folks if you like this video you know what to do smash that like button and get subscribed not only does it show your appreciation for the insane amount of work that goes into making these videos but as I always say it makes my mother very proud not many folks by the way have followed me on Twitter Instagram or Tick Tock so please do so links Below on Twitter especially I talk a lot about upcoming Tech that I'm working on anyway go do something awesome with your day and I will catch you later

titulo: Best Budget Laptop: HP Pavilion Plus 14
transcricao: Tech family the HP Pavilion plus 14 inch laptop is the best laptop that I've ever used under a thousand US Dollars full stop end of story it is the only laptop to get almost all the basics right in that price range and this is the laptop most of my viewers should buy so long as you don't need powerful dedicated graphics or long battery life let me explain why starting with the display it is absolutely stunning and a joy to look at both my two units came with a 14 inch OLED 2880 by 1800 panel colors are extremely accurate and brightness Peaks that are very respectable 400 nits content looks Vivid and sharp and I was able to comfortably run the laptop at 175 window scaling this allowed me to see more information on screen than with a default 200 percent combined with a 16 by 10 aspect ratio in my Excel test I was able to see 38 rows on screen which is decent enough to get real work done oh and scrolling and other movement on screen looks super smooth due to the 90hz fresh right the only thing that I don't like is that pwm is used to lower the brightness on this display that's where the screen turns on and off the backlight very fast so the screen becomes less bright Honestly though the PW and flickering in this laptop it really isn't too bad compared to other laptops that I've tested that use this method so most people won't have an issue with it oh and talking about brightness you may notice that the laptop seems to lower and raise the brightness at random when on battery this is actually a supposed feature to help improve battery life by optimizing the display's brightness in attempts to change the brightness based on the content shown on screen a very good idea but in practice it doesn't work so well if this feature annoys you like it did me you can easily turn it off in the system display brightness section by expanding it and unselecting the checkbox the display is also glossy which you probably noticed significant Reflections in my b-roll in everyday use though the screen gets bright enough that I really didn't notice the Reflections at all overall I think my assistant summed up this display perfectly when she said the screen is better than the Razer Blade 14s that cost more than double this laptop all the keyboard is your typical HP one that you find in many of their Pavilion and edv laptops which means it is a good one comfortable enough to type on with decent key travel I know some people do like having the page up down Etc Keys placed down the right side of the keyboard but for me the keyboard feels a little off balance with the keys there and I sometimes mishit them the only major issue with this keyboard is that HP continues to combine light colored keys with a light colored backlight this makes the characters insanely hard to make out when the backlight is on and viewed from an angle this happens to me during the day when I'm using the laptop propped up on my lap you'll frequently have to toggle the backlight off in these situations to see the keys perhaps these laptops are more likely to sell with this clean silver looking keyboard aesthetic but I'd take the higher contrast dark colored keys of Apple's laptops over this any day as their keyboards don't have this issue the trackpad is good enough tracking is reasonably smooth although not the smoothest I've used but it's still accurate The Click feels good too however I do want to be transparent about one thing when my first review unit arrived I ended up shipping it straight by UPS ground Across America I did that so I could work on this review while on vacation yes I do that when UPS delivered it I noticed an issue the trackpad kept getting stuck when I was using the laptop on my lap while resting my Palms with some force on the palm rest I reached out to HP and they sent me a second unit no issue whatsoever I did search if anyone else had reported this issue and so far they haven't so I'm assuming it's either a one-off or caused by my UPS shipping in the event that you do buy one and it happens to have that issue just have HP swap it out the port selection is very decent for a small laptop you've got two USB type-c ports on the 10 gigabit variety that both support charging unfortunately neither support the faster Thunderbolt transfer rates you've then got two USB a ports an HDMI 2.1 Port as well as a headphone mic combo Jack I didn't even used to mention the headphone port on my prior reviews as it was so standard but since Dell decided to remove it in the XPS 13 plus I thought I'd mention it the Pavilion plus also has a Micro SD card reader one downside is that both charging capable ports are on the right side so you will have to run a cable around the back if your power outlet is on the other side of the laptop by the way there is a fingerprint reader which works well and will get you logged in fast the speakers are so so they do get very loud but when they go above 80 decibels the sound completely breaks apart and sounds extremely muddy and outright awful below 80 decibels though they are passable albeit a little muddy sounding still [Music] [Music] here is how the webcam looks and sounds in the best possible lighting conditions by the way the laptop as a whole looks good enough yeah yes its chassis does seem a bit dated by today's standards you won't find any striking Design Elements here but guess what you won't find any sacrifices here either like those on the Dell XPS 13 plus or the fingerprint magnet MacBook Air M2 in the midnight color it's just a stock standard silver laptop it also doesn't feel as high quality as more expensive ones but it's sturdy enough plus it's super lightweight for a 14 inch laptop at around three pounds that makes it very comfortable to use on your lap while that and the lack of heat you feel and fan noise you hear while using it which brings me to Performance both my units have the Intel 12gen i7 12700h processor with 16 gig of RAM and a one terabyte SSD in geekbench which tests variety of common performance tasks The Pavilion plus 14 performed very well in single core applications however it underperformed in multi-core especially compared to the Lenovo slim 7i Pro X which has the same Intel CPU it did perform better than the ryzen laptops six thousand and five thousand series CPUs though switching to Center bench which tests how the laptop performs under Max load in this case it performed very well a little worse than the slim 7i Pro X with the same CPU and better than almost all the ryzen CPUs I have tested to date with the exception of running the Asus G14 in turbo mode which by the way is an unbearable experience as its fans spin insanely loud when you do that back on the Pavilion plus if you do run the laptop in Balance mode performance can't be sustained over long running tasks you'll need to run it in performance mode to do that you can switch modes in hp's commands in a software I did try running the laptop in the highest performance mode while on battery power and unfortunately it isn't able to give you the same performance as when the laptop is plugged into the wall looking at Power draw the laptop bursts at 61 watts of power but then sustains at 45 for the performance mode and I measured a lower 33 for balance mode this explains the difference in cinebench scores here are the clock speeds I recorded during this test and also the CPU temperatures looking at heat you'd feel when the laptop is doing high performance tasks it did very well in Balance mode remaining only somewhat warm to the touch it did get a bit hotter when running its performance mode though and now Fair noise when the laptop is under full load here it did very well particularly in Balance mode substantially better than Lenovo slim 7i Pro X with the same CPU looking at these results I'd strongly advise you run the laptop in Balance mode unless you are doing a lot of sustained long-running performance tasks it offers plenty of performance for very acceptable heat and fan noise in Balance mode that is by the way I didn't test graphical intensive tasks as I don't have the model with a dedicated RTX 2050 graphics and the integrated Graphics in the CPU I have is very poor you won't be able to do any video editing or intensive AAA gaming on this configuration older titles and Esports games only switching to light use such as browsing the web watching video and writing documents in this case the laptop absolutely shines there is literally no fan noise at all and the laptop remains comfortably cool to the touch it is the only Intel laptop that I've used that you don't hear fan noise or feel heat while on a zoom call HP really have done a standout job here in light use this laptop destroys lenovo's yoga slim 7i Pro X with the same Intel H series CPU as well as my ryzen laptops which like the Pro X feel warm to the touch and you often hear fan noise using the Pavilion plus 14 feels more like using a MacBook with an M series chip seriously HP I don't know what you've done but it's fantastic other than one thing battery life battery life on this laptop is not great around 5 hours I tested both my two units setting them for the best possible battery life in both windows and HP software I then set the display on each laptop to around 200 nits of brightness at 60 hertz I then ran a Netflix show on repeat over Wi-Fi for 4. hours one laptop had 21 remaining and the other 15 percent by the way I accidentally originally ran the test leaving the screen at a 90 Hertz refresh rate which was a mistake I recorded less battery on that test so definitely ensure you set the screen to 60 hertz if you want the best possible battery results and on that note you will get more battery life if you turn the screen's brightness down further this laptop's poor battery life isn't surprising as we all know that Intel's 12th gen processors aren't efficient like Intel claims and in hp's case they have put the high performance H series processor inside which are normally reserved for larger laptops and paired it with only a 51 watt hour battery you really need a larger battery to get decent battery life out of this processor if you do want a bit better battery life I'd consider buying this laptop configured with one of the u-series processors that it is offered with anyway make sure you bring your charger with you which might I add is larger than I think it should be HB supplies this laptop with a 91 USBC charger which is bigger in size and the higher wattage 100 watt charger that Lenovo supplies with their yoga slim 7 Pro X this adds to the carry weight of this laptop which is unfortunate because the laptop itself is super light honestly as you don't need 90 watts of power for most use cases on this laptop I go straight out and buy a smaller lighter 65 watt charger for it like the super small one that Lenovo supplies with some of their think pads I didn't cover this but the RAM is soldered the SSD and Wi-Fi card they are replaceable let's finish with pricing this is where this laptop just blows it out of the park at the time of this review this laptop starts at a ludicrously low 579 US dollars for the I5 model with 8 gig of RAM a 256g SSD and a non OLED display my review unit with the i7 12700h 60 gig of RAM one terabyte SSD and the OLED display is 999 dollars and for a hundred dollars more you can get the laptop with an Nvidia RTE X 2050 at this price range this laptop just cannot be beaten it is simply the best laptop under a thousand US Dollars I've ever reviewed especially now that Apple's MacBook Air which used to dominate the sub a thousand dollar price range for the older M1 version that is is now significantly more expensive for the new M2 version as essentially if you buy with 512 gig of storage or more oh and keep an eye out for coupons or student discounts when you buy like those that are posted in the laptop deal sections on Reddit look I talk a lot about this in my videos you want a laptop that just gets the basics right with as few conscious as possible and the Pavilion plus 14 it does that it's got a great screen it's plenty powerful it doesn't get warm to the touch while using it you don't hear fan noise the keyboard is very comfortable the trackpad is good enough it's lightweight and the price is super competitive this is the laptop that most of you should be buying so long as you don't need powerful dedicated graphics or long battery life Heck if my budget was less than a thousand US Dollars this is the laptop that I would personally buy and that means a lot coming from me because you know me I'm super tough to please well that's all for today folks if you like this video you know what to do smash that like button and get subscribed not only does it show your appreciation for the insane amount of work that goes into making these but as I always say it makes my mother very proud I'll post links to my Instagram Twitter and Tick Tock down below for plenty of behind the scenes coverage till next time go do something awesome with your day and I will catch you later

titulo: @Apple Macbook Air (M2) Review: Almost Perfect!
transcricao: all right tech family the macbook air with apple's new m2 chip is good really good let's get into it i bought the cheaper of the two models available the 8 core cpu and ecourt gpu one which i chose as going into this review i didn't believe that this laptop should be bought for high performance tasks i would prefer it performed better i less heat more battery life in more casual tasks that i would actually use it for such as office work and browsing the web and you see lower end less power intensive chips tend to do this i then configured my unit with a larger 512gb of storage i felt that 256gb would be too small for me by the way i always buy laptops in a config i would actually consider keeping for myself if they turn out to be awesome i just feel like it helps me review laptops as an actual owner plus i had read reviews that the 256 gig drive was substantially slower than the larger capacity models i didn't end up upgrading the ram from 8 gig as with the processor i didn't feel for the use case i expected for this laptop i was going to need it finally i chose the silver model i was tempted to buy that midnight color the new one but saw other reviewers saying it was a fingerprint magnet and i just don't want to have to deal with that on receiving the laptop the first thing i noticed was that it looks stunning apple's new design language really comes alive with this super thin chassis i didn't think the macbook pro 14 and 16 looked as stunning as something like the razer blade 14 but the thinness of the air just really makes this design pop it looks incredibly stylish i do like the addition of the magsafe port it means i don't have to use one of the usb-c ports for power like i had to on the older version both the usb-c ports do support charging still my only knit is that all charging capable ports are on the left side so you will have to run a cable around the back if your outlet is on the other side of the laptop the display is noticeably larger than on the prior model at 13.6 inches it felt large enough that i didn't feel like i was using a super small laptop it's bright and color accurate too when compared to the macbook pro 14 best of the best display content on this one is not as crisp or vivid one minor negative about this display is that normally on apple laptops i'm able to comfortably write at the more space setting allowing me to see more content on screen the amount of content that you can see on screen without needing to squint depends on several factors the pixel density brightness contrast etc i wasn't able to quite use the more space setting on this laptop not without zooming on documents on individual applications like word or excel on excel i was able to see 43 rows on screen which is still good for a 13 inch laptop by the way the notch really shouldn't be this large because of its size and the smaller 13-inch screen it does take away space from apps that run in the menu bar this menu bar is where mac os puts running apps that don't need to use the full screen an example would be dropbox this is an important area for mac os this laptop doesn't have as much visible space for these apps because of the large notch that being said in everyday use honestly the notch just blends into the background and you likely won't notice it the keyboard is the main thing that i really don't like about this laptop it feels noticeably low travel i found it a little uncomfortable especially compared to the macbook pro 14 and 16 keyboard those feel deeper the dell xps 13 plus also feels substantially more comfortable to type on than this laptop the trackpad is excellent as always with apple laptops the sound is very good for a laptop this size i was expecting that it wouldn't be good as there are no visible speaker grilles on the laptop but i was wrong it was better than all the windows laptops that i've tested however not as good as the macbook pro 14. here's how the webcam on the macbook air looks and sounds in excellent lighting conditions the performance on this laptop is incredible so much better than i could have imagined in everyday use this laptop is very snappy it also never gets hot or even warm to the touch this was an issue on my prime macbook air with m1 my assumption is that this redesigned chassis is better able to dissipate heat from the processor anyway it remained very cool to the touch in everyday use and of course dead silent no annoying fan noise here i did try editing one simple 4k video project on the laptop in premiere pro and it performed like an absolute champ this is awesome considering that my unit only has 8 gig of ram on that note i was concerned that eight gig wouldn't be enough but it was totally fine for my use case that's where i was regularly running about 10 to 20 browser tabs open on chrome citrix is running dropbox discord and numerous office applications i saw no slowdown whatsoever even when editing that video project no slowdown switching between apps or anything else so don't beat yourself up for not paying that ludicrous price for the 16 gig of ram upgrade you may not need it honestly overall i was blown away with how well this laptop performs in comparison something like the latest dell xps 9320 with intel's 12th gen isn't as snappy and feels substantially warmer to the touch in light use and there is zero chance zero that that laptop could edit the same 4k video project that this one could let's take a look at some performance tests for a bit more color in geekbench which tests a variety of common performance tasks this laptop scored the highest single core performance i've ever seen single core performance is still one of the primary factors in what makes an application snappy multi-core performance was also very good a nice step up from the prior generation but not quite hitting the heights of intel's 12th gen p-series equipped ultrabooks like the dell xps 13 plus moving on to cinebench which tests the laptop when the processor is maxed out again similar story to geekbench it trails the intel 12 gen laptops and now amd ryzen 5000 series 2 from last year however those laptops have substantial fan noise for the performance which this laptop just does not it is still a very nice bump up in performance though compared to the prior generation m1 when running cinebench on a lip for 10 minutes yes like other reviewers i did notice a drop in performance but honestly what can you expect this laptop has no fan to call the processor the only way it can be called is to throttle it yes performance drops but not a monolithic one i've seen worse on intel 12-gen laptops that have fans low power consumption continues to be a strong point for the m series of processors which is what enables this laptop to perform without a fan this laptop requires around half the wattage as an intel 12 gen processor a p series one that is yet it has far better performance per watt i mean heck the new dell xps 13 plus comes with a 60 watt charger this laptop's charging is half of that at 30 watts when it comes to heat you feel when the processor is under sustained heavy load it gets warm for sure but it doesn't get as warm to the touches intel 12th gen laptops seriously to edit videos as smoothly as this laptop does for a windows one you'd probably need at least 100 watts of power fed to the laptop if not more and that laptop would run loud and feel warm the laptop is very portable it feels noticeably lighter than the macbook pro 4t and is very comfortable to use on your lap or carry around with you one of the best things about the prime macbook air with m1 was it was only slightly more expensive than a budget laptop you could easily find it for around 900 us dollars for the quality that you were getting it was a no-brainer and was the clear value for money winner it was the laptop that i recommended for most people that didn't have a very specific use case i.e say gaming however this generation of macbook air now starts two hundred dollars more and right now it can't be found as easily on sale so it's really three hundred dollars more plus in 2022 the 256 gig drive it includes really isn't ideal you really need to upgrade it to 512 gig so you're looking at spending around 1 400 us dollars at that price point it's no longer the clear winner there are several other good laptops to consider which brings me to my conclusion this laptop is awesome far better than i ever thought but it's no longer the laptop i'd recommend to most people for example i used to suggest that those on a tighter budget looking to spend around 700 us dollars try to save to get the macbook air with m1 as it was a lot better than pc laptops at that price point but in 2022 there are plenty of good windows laptops now available sub a thousand dollars like the hp pavilion plus this laptop is really for those who want an excellent all-around premium laptop a student for example who has money or their parents do an office worker someone learning to code someone doing very lightweight video editing i'd think twice though at buying this laptop if you intend to configure it with higher specs the higher end model of this laptop with 16 gig of ram will cost around 1 700 us dollars at that amount you're almost at the price of the macbook pro 14. that laptop screen is a far more useful size especially for people looking at a lot of information on screen like a software developer or financial analyst plus it's substantially more powerful for high performance tasks and it has a more comfortable keyboard you could also look at the asus g14 which costs less at around 1 500 us dollars and is a more powerful machine allowing you to do things that this one can't like aaa gaming obviously with the asus g14 and macbook pro 14 you'll be sacrificing a bit of portability as they are larger laptops still portable though for me personally when it comes to a premium portable laptop i'm going to stick with the xps 13 plus 9320 due to its more comfortable keyboard for my use case for this kind of laptop i do a ton of typing and value that above titulo: Dell XPS 13 Plus (9320) Review
transcricao: all right tech family i've been using the dell xps 13 plus solidly for weeks and i'd like to share my thoughts with you if you've been watching my channel for a while you'll know that i'm extremely familiar with these xps 13 laptops for years they've been my daily driver if you saw me out in a coffee store you'd see me using an xps 13. i loved their portability excellent screen surprisingly comfortable keyboard and accurate trackpad my first xps was the 9370 in rose gold with intel's 8th gen chip i eventually switched the 9300 model which was a major refresh to the xps line it heralded in the form factor of the laptop that you see in front of me today a larger 16 by 10 aspect ratio screen and at the time intel's long-awaited 10th gen chip that model unfortunately was a disaster the intel chip ran way too hot for the tiny laptop to cool luckily soon after dell came out with the xbs 13 9310 which had intel's much improved 11th gen tiger light chip this made the laptop usable when it came to temperatures you would actually feel but even with intel's 11th gen chip the xps still felt quite warm to the touch even for lightweight tasks and it couldn't really run anything that intensive that's because even though the xms had a powerful processor inside the cooling solution just couldn't call it properly no matter what dell's marketing and pr departments tell you and yes dell provides you with an array of thermal modes to run the laptop including cool ultra performance quiet etc but they all sucked because fundamentally they just throw the problem somewhere else you can't escape physics cool mode did indeed keep your laptop cool but you get throttled performance and loud fan noise quiet mode kept the fan silent but then you get a warm feeling laptop and severely throttled performance so gather around and let me tell you if this new xps 13 plus improves on its predecessors and whether this laptop should be at the top of your wishlist if you're seeking a premium high-powered portable one let's start with the keyboard as it's changed substantially this year you've got a touch sensitive area for the function buttons and a slightly changed layout the backspace key has been shifted to the left to make room for a power fingerprint reader combo button the good news is that this keyboard is still one of the most comfortable low trouble ones around the keys have this soft touch feeling that just makes them quite delightful a joy to use however if you do type with a degree of force you'll feel the keys bottoming out and becoming a little uncomfortable i originally thought i would hate the new touch sensitive function area i had nightmares that my experience using it would match that of apple's dreadful touch bar where you'd often mishit the button you intended to but this was nowhere near as bad the keys don't change their location and purpose when you switch between applications like they do on the touch bar so your muscle memory still works in fact for everyday use like writing the script for this very video i didn't feel i missed the physical function buttons all that much other than perhaps the escape key which had occasionally mishit that being said if you're someone who uses the function buttons a lot like a data scientist using excel this change is going to annoy you i do appreciate the beautiful design of this keyboard but this is unnecessary form over function dell's normal keys look pretty enough and their product management team should have known better put back the physical function keys no one asked for this change i had a similar experience with this power fingerprint reader combo button pushing the backspace key to the left from where it is normally placed like the function row i didn't mind it nearly as much as i thought but it's not the ideal placement the new trackpad that blends in with the palm rest is excellent seriously i've literally got nothing else to say about it it works a dream and is one of the best trackpads available on any pc laptop the display options haven't changed that much from the prior generation which isn't bad the 4k plus resolution display available on this laptop has always surprised me as to how much information i can see on the small screen without needing to squint this is due to its high brightness excellent pixel density aspect ratio etc but laptop displays are something that we've seen a lot of improvements in recently high refresh rate panels mini led panels etc the ips panel in this display just feels a little dated in comparison it doesn't have the contrast of an oled or mini led panel and i saw some very slight backlight bleeding on my screen which doesn't occur on those other displays by the way you can purchase this laptop with an oled panel but you do lose a bit of brightness for that and it just isn't as good as the mini led panel in the macbook pro 14 which is brighter and has a higher 120 hertz refresh rate that high refresh rate gives you super smooth movement on screen the xps panel options are only available with a max 60 hertz refresh rate let's switch gears and talk about how this laptop performs with its new intel 12-gen processor as that really is one of the most important things to discuss by the way i actually bought both the i7i5 models and i'm going to do an even deeper performance comparison of these two 12th gen chips in another video so make sure you're subscribed for that one whether you buy the i7 or i5 chip in this laptop what you need to know is that the laptop feels incredibly snappy and performs very well in short running tasks it's also extremely quiet in everyday use you almost never hear fan noise but the cons are it gets quite warm to the touch particularly the underside of the laptop and performance drops noticeably in long-running tasks let me back this up with some data here are my geekbench scores which test a variety of common performance tasks you can see this laptop performs insanely well and here are my cinebench results which tests how the processor performs when maxed out again extremely good however in tasks that run any longer than a couple of seconds the laptop's performance drops dramatically you can see these big drops when i run a cinebench r23 test on a loop for 10 minutes these performance drops are noticeable on the laptop's default optimize mode which is the mode i recommend you run the laptop on more on that later the issue is that a lot of the increase in performance of intel's 12 gen processors is due to an increase in power draw not efficiency improvements of the processor as the cooling solution hasn't been improved dramatically on this laptop this additional power draw leads to a very warm feeling laptop particularly on the underside surprisingly the temperatures you feel on the keyboard deck when under load are tolerable and an improvement over prior xps laptops dell does offer an ultra performance mode by the way which can mostly maintain the laptop's high performance for a duration of time but it comes at a substantial increase in fan noise in fact when it comes to dell's thermal modes like prior generations of xps laptops they all pass the issue around dell's cool mode makes the laptop cool to the touch but increases the fan noise quiet mode on the other hand drops the performance a lot you get the picture honestly i'd recommend it just leaving it on the default optimize mode in my opinion it has the best balance of performance fan noise and temperatures you'd actually feel what i think is more important though is how this laptop performs in everyday use my gut is that most people will use these laptops for more casual tasks like browsing the web office work etc in this scenario this laptop performs very well and is extremely quiet however it still feels very warm to the touch especially when comparing it to apple's macbooks with their incredibly efficient m-series chips you really are going to notice the difference in heat you feel between these machines the apple laptops are far cooler than the touch and are therefore more comfortable to use look overall performance is much improved from the prior generation of xps laptops for little downside might i say so it is definitely a win but in 2022 intel is just uncompetitive with apple when it comes to processors they are trying to sell these processors with strong benchmark results but in reality these benchmarks are for short running tasks not continuous ones in the real world apple has a substantial lead by the way you may have noticed on one of my slides that this laptop can draw up to 58 watts of power since it only comes with a 60 watt charger i was worried it would drain the battery when under load if we do the math 58 watts of power to the processor plus power to the screen and other parts of the laptop you'll easily be drawing more than the 60 watt charger can provide i tested this scenario a lot and the good news is this issue doesn't occur this laptop doesn't draw that 458 watts of power for more than a couple of seconds or so two negatives i'd like to bring to your attention i noticed during my use that neither of my xps 9320 laptops sit 100 flat when on a table when i place my palms down on the laptop you can hear the laptop creak also on both laptops the keyboard backlight is not evenly lit and too dim on several keys namely the tab and backspace key dell has a history of quality control issues and they seem to have carried across here these ones are minor but know what you'd hoped for on a premium laptop by the way my battery life results will be in my upcoming video comparing the xps i5 and i7 processors together and on that note let me give you my concluding thoughts on the dell xps 13 plus 9320 it is definitely a step forward from prior generations of xps 13s for sure it looks more visually stunning the laptop feels noticeably snappier in everyday use and it is dead quiet for tasks like office work browsing the web etc when it comes to processor intensive tasks the laptop has plenty of power if those tasks are short running like doing a quick code compile or you can deal with the side effects of running the laptop in ultra performance mode which bumps up the fan noise and warmth of the chassis the main issue with this laptop is that for people looking for a high-powered portable premium laptop the macbook pro 14 is just far superior it runs much cooler to the touch than this laptop and i mean much its screen is larger brighter has greater contrast and a faster refresh rate the graphics capabilities of that laptop allow you to do things that this one couldn't even dream about like editing 4k videos the speakers on that laptop destroy the speakers on this one [Music] the webcam is much better the keyboard is more comfortable the battery life runs circles around this laptop and it isn't that much more expensive than this xps that's if you spec up an apples to apples configuration ie1 with 16gb ram and a high resolution display even at the lower end of the xps's price point you are now competing with apple's excellent macbook pro 13 and macbook air which like the 14 are better than this laptop in many ways but i still think for some people this xps 9320 is a very viable choice let's say you want an extremely lightweight laptop that runs windows or linux and you don't want to sacrifice much performance plus if you are predominantly using it either plugged into an external monitor keyboard and mouse or on a desk you are getting a ton of the laptop's benefits while avoiding a lot of its cons but at the end of the day as someone who personally is a target consumer of premium powerful portable laptops if i could only have one of these two i'd definitely choose the macbook pro 14 over the xbs 13 plus 9320 well that's all for today folks if you like this video you know what to do smash that like button and get subscribed not only does it show your appreciation for the insane amount of work that goes into making these but as i always say it makes my mother very proud if you need help with the decision on which laptop to purchase make sure to check out my discord channel where vetted laptop specialists are standing by to help you out till next time go do something awesome with your day and i will catch you later

transcricao: tech family as someone who mostly reviews laptops the number one question that i get asked is what laptop should i buy specifically from people who just want a good quality laptop that doesn't break the bank to be used for casual tasks checking email working remotely studying browsing the web etc nothing that requires a high powered device just simple tasks so when parent left a comment about this new asus laptop with a 14 inch high resolution oled panel paired with intel's 12 gen processor and available at best buy for under 800 us dollars i got super excited and when i consider the best buy often has regular rotating sales dropping the prices of most laptops by up to 200 us dollars my excitement was amplified so i went straight out to best buy to buy it my best buy configuration comes with intel's 12th gen i5 1240p processor a gig of ddr5 ram and a 256 gig ssd it's listed for a price of 749 us dollars note asus does mention higher spec variants with say 16 gig of ram on their website look as an experiment i'm going to do this review a little differently from my prior ones i'm first going to tell you the good things about this laptop and then afterwards i'll tell you the negatives that you'll have to deal with if you buy it by the way let me know in the comments below if you like this new style of review from me let's get into the positives for the kind of user who should be buying this laptop a casual user that is there is a lot to love the first thing that you'll notice is the chassis it looks very stylish you've got this slick modern unique styling on the lid and it's in this gorgeous dark blue color the construction feels high quality certainly well above most laptops in the price range and its weight is quite decent not as good as exceptionally light laptops like the x1 nano or the ideapad carbon but certainly very portable the screen is exceptional especially for a laptop in this price range in fact most price ranges a gorgeous bright oled panel with near perfect color reproduction it's a high resolution 2880x1800 display it has a fast 90hz refresh rate so movement looks super smooth on screen and that desirable 16 by 10 aspect ratio so you'll see a bit more information for applications that go down the page honestly this screen is an absolute dream other than one thing which i'll cover in the cons to test how well the screen actually performs i.e how much information i can comfortably see on it i set window scaling at an amount i was able to see the most amount of content on screen without needing to squint to help me compare with other laptops i counted the number of rows i could see in excel which on this laptop is 40. this is a good result for a small laptop the only laptops that substantially beat it were the macbook pro 14 and larger 15-inch laptops by the way apple laptops have always outperformed pc laptops in this test the mac operating system just does an excellent job of showing a large amount of information on screen the next thing you'll like is the keyboard although it isn't the most comfortable laptop keyboard i've used in this price range it's very good the layout is excellent every key is in the optimal place for example just look at where the arrow keys are no stupid keys that you might miss hit above the left and right arrow like some laptops have or shifting the whole keyboard to the left to make way for another column of keys the backlight works well and there is a handy fingerprint reader in the power button that will get you logged in fast the only thing that holds this keyboard back is that the keys feel a little low travel you will feel them bottom out as you type moving on to the trackpad the trackpad itself is decent it's large smooth and perfectly usable it's certainly not the most accurate trackpad i've used on a windows laptop but in the price range it's good enough one issue that i want to call out is with the numberpad trackpad this is a feature of asus laptops but i found that it would frequently just switch to this mode when i was using it as a regular trackpad this was very annoying however i found that it can be permanently turned off in asus's included customization software the port selection on this laptop is likely the best you'll get on any small laptop you've got one usb port of the faster 10 gigabit variety you've got two thunderbolt 4 ports that both support charging one hdmi 2.0 b port a micro sd card reader and a headphone mic combo jack onto performance performance for lightweight tasks such as writing up an assignment for school browsing the web using citrix to log into a work computer etc etc was all excellent you can see the laptop's geekbench scores on screen substantially better than the ryzen 5000 series processors and almost on par with intel's older 11th gen h series used in much larger heavier high-powered laptops however keep in mind geekbench does not really push the cpu as ryzen 5 800u processor and as you'll recall from the prior graph it doesn't perform quite as well as that processor when the processor is fully utilized it also requires 50 more power than intel's to overflowing that extra memory needed to the laptop's mechanical hard drive a process known as swapping those hard disks were super slow in today's world pcie ssds even the one in this laptop are substantially faster and have way lower latency plus operating systems now compress files in ram anyway which makes your ram go further look as mentioned earlier i'm talking about people doing lightweight tasks if you are a software developer for instance don't buy this laptop even running a single virtual machine or containerized application could be a problem if your heart is truly set on
