titulo: HP Omen Review (Ryzen 4800H + GTX 1660 Ti) - A BEAST of a laptop that I bought for myself!!!
transcricao: Tech Family, I am excited, it's not every day that I buy a laptop for myself. But one of the main reasons I started this channel was because I personally was on the hunt for the highest powered portable laptop that runs cool, quiet and looks great. And I wanted to share that journey with you. Seriously, check the intro of my initial videos from this time last year on the channel. What makes it so hard for me to find a laptop is because I cross many high-end use cases. I edit 4k video, I program, and I gain. And I do all this on the go. Plus, I'm super fussy when it comes to fan noise, heat and a good screen. Let me tell you why I was on the hunt for a new laptop. I have been using the MacBook Pro 16 for video editing and programming. I know a lot of YouTubers will tell you the MacBook Pro 16 can handle 4k video. And yes, they would be correct. But my videos have multiple camera angles, all recording 4k, B-roll, effects, etc. My upgraded MacBook Pro 16 was being pushed to its limits. The laptop was heating up to uncomfortable levels and there were tons of drop frames during editing. My Aero 17 on the other hand does have a better cooling solution than the MacBook Pro. And far better graphics. But it is annoyingly loud, even when not under load. It's fans pulsate, which means they turn on and off. And they are high pitched, which is super noticeable even on quiet mode. Heck, when I try to re-record a voiceover, I have to power down the laptop completely. Also, when I do a hardware based render, there were erroneous artifacts in the video, causing me to have to re-render it using the slower software mode. That's why my Aero spends most of its life in a drawer, other than when I use it for gaming. So, I've been on the hunt for a new laptop. What I wanted was a step up in power so I could edit without drop frames. I also wanted a laptop that was quiet. I don't want to be distracted by fan noise when doing light tasks. Plus, I want to try streaming and don't want to laptop with fans so loud that they can be heard through the mic. I also needed more than one terabyte of storage. My MacBook Pro 16 has a terabyte in and has been the bane of my existence. Each one of my videos needs around 200 gig of storage. Plus my B-roll library that I frequently look through is 500 gig. I was constantly having to move files around to free up space, which is such a waste of time. I also wanted the laptop to run cool to the touch. You might say, Josh, why don't you build a desktop? Up until now, I live in a small apartment that doesn't have a desk. I didn't have room for one. However, I am moving to a bigger apartment with plenty of space. But, I run a YouTube channel that has a laptop focus to it. I think it's super important that I perform real high-end tasks on the laptop so I can give you accurate information on what they are like. Maybe one day, I'll expand to covering desktops, but not right now. Originally, I was eyeing the new Alienware M17 R3, the 8 core Intel 10th-gen processor with a 2080 Super graphics card. I heard its calling solution had been improved and was excited to game with such graphics. But, it was a pretty big device. And, at $3,000 with 32 gig of soldered RAM and an Intel CPU, my heart wasn't in it. I really wanted a high-end AMD CPU with a strong Nvidia graphics card, like most of us right now. I was also considering the updated Aero 17 for 2020, but they didn't change the calling solution. It'll probably have all the issues of my model. And, I did buy the XPS 17, but it drained the battery like crazy while performing high-end tasks, so I returned it. By the way, I was planning to get my new laptop with a 4K screen for editing on the go and a high refresh rate monitor for the new apartment to take advantage of the graphics while gaming. But, everything changed when I was invest by looking at laptops that you asked me to check out. I saw the HBO moment and fell in love with it. The first thing I noticed was the screen, super bright, great colors and the white balance looked cold. I love screens with the cold or white balance. I normally check the keyboard and palm rest of laptops in stores to see how warm they are. If they are warm running the demo that they run on repeat in the store all day, then they are certainly going to be too warm for me when I put some load on them. The Omen, however, was cold to the touch. Plus, it had that perfect combination. A powerful AMD processor paired with a high-end Nvidia dedicated graphics card. All for a little over $1,000 US dollars. So, 5 minutes later, I was walking out of Best Buy as a proud owner of one. Unfortunately, another 5 minutes later, I realized I had bought the wrong model with 8GB RAM and a 512GB SSD. Rather than the slightly more expensive one with 16GB RAM and a 1TB SSD. As Best Buy classifies in exchange like this as a return, I decided to just buy the other model as well. So, in this review, I'll also tell you if there are any noticeable manufacturing differences. When I got home, I first checked the displays. Both units have surprisingly good panels, with great colors, clocking in at 99% SIGB. They are also very bright at above 300 Nits. And as they have matte displays which aren't reflective being above 300 Nits makes the Omen very usable in a bright environment. Neither of my units had any dead pixels, however, I did notice some differences between the panels. The model with 16GB RAM had a panel that was brighter with better contrast. But I noticed it had some backlight bleed. Whereas the panel in the 8GB model had no bleed, which is rare on an IPS display. I'd show you, but it didn't really sharpen my long exposure photo. By the way, they both use the same LG panel LGD05 FE. The panels do have a 144 Hertz refresh rate which is awesome and aren't grainy at all which is good for a matte display. When it comes to performance, this laptop is an absolute beast and that is an understatement. What makes it even more impressive is it runs super cool and quiet. Let me show you. In Centrebench R20, which really pushes the CPU, it annihilates the competition. A score of 4400 is bonkers. Nothing can catch it. Not the 17 inch Dell XPS with its Intel 8 core 10th Gen CPU, nor the MacBook Pro 16 8 core or the Aero 17. Take a look at this. To get the Aero 17 close to that score, I had to undervolt it, overclock it, run it and allow fan profile, user calling pad and call my mother. Even then, it can't touch the HP Omen score and the Omen can beat it in its default fan profile, which isn't that loud. I mean, have a look at how quiet the Omen is in comparison to all these other high-end Intel laptops. Now, take a look at the temperatures that you would actually feel. This laptop runs super cool. Even the CPU temps destroy the competition and Geekbench scores tell the same story. Performance like this was precisely what I was looking for, especially as this laptop is just so cool and quiet. Alright, graphics. This laptop has a full powered 660 Ti, no maxed-tube. It puts in some impressive scores. Here is Fire Strike, and now Time Spy. Now, let's zoom in on just the GPU score of Time Spy. What you'll notice is it performs similar to the RTX 2060 in the Dell XPS 9700, and it doesn't use up your battery while doing so like the XPS 17 does. So, props to HP for understanding how much power their laptop actually needs. For gaming, I had no problems maxing out hitting the 144 FPS on League of Legends, and for the AAA game Borderlands 3, I got a little less than 60 FPS on the highest possible settings. Dropping settings down saw me hit frames of around 70 FPS for high, and well above that in medium. All in all, this laptop can run AAA games. As I'm moving apartments in three days, I didn't run my full set of real-world tests. However, I did run a Premiere Pro export test, as that's a primary task I expect to use the laptop for. No surprises, it was faster than the competition. To be honest, I'm pretty confident this laptop would crush all the real-world tests I would normally throw at it. Audio latency was surprisingly good, and I actually loaded the League of Legends client while running the test, which is a pretty intensive task. The laptop comes with WiFi 6 and performs very fast as expected. On the SSD front, both drives a super speedy and so is the RAM, which runs at 3200 MHz in your channel. By the way, even my 8GB of RAM model has dual channel RAM, which is good. You can upgrade both the SSD and RAM. A couple of important notes here. Even though the back of the laptop seems easy to take off, it isn't. There are a lot of clips holding the back in place. I broke some when opening the laptop. Be careful, I'll post a link to the spludging kit I used in the description below. Now, Ryzen does not use Intel XMP, so many RAM kits do not run at their advertised speeds, which I found out the hard way. I ordered a Ballistics and HyperX kit that were both advertised at 3200 MHz. The Ballistics run at 2666 and the HyperX at 2400. Props to Jared for passing along a helpful article that lists RAM that will work at the advertised speed for AMD. Link in the description below. I ended up buying a different Crucial 32GB of RAM kit, which worked well. Some more good news. There is a second M.2 slot available, which is great, as I put in a 2TB Samsung 970 EVO Plus drive. So, with three terabytes of space, the storage problem of mine is finally solved. The chassis, as a whole, feels well constructed, and the lid does open with one hand. But when you look closely, there are manufacturing issues that you don't see in laptops like the MacBook Pro 16. For example, the right side of the trackpad is a little more depressed than the left on both units. Also, the hinge on the left side of my 16GB RAM one doesn't look parallel and is kind of at an angle compared to the right. But honestly, the price of these laptops is so low for the incredible value you get, so I'm going to give HBO Pass here. I was worried that the somewhat sharp edge of the front of the laptop would be uncomfortable on my wrist, but it wasn't at all. Also, you're going to be wiping these laptops down a lot because they are fingerprint magnets. The ports are ample, which is great, with HDMI, Ethernet, Mini Display, 3UPA and 1UPC. It doesn't have Thunderbolt as this is an AMD laptop and that's Intel tech. Hopefully soon we'll get AMD laptops with USB 4, which will offer those same speeds. The SD card reader is very slow, so I'll continue to use an external one. However, I'd rather have one in the laptop than not just in case. Also, the USB ports are all the slower gen 1, which is unfortunate. Here's how the webcam looks and sounds, honestly, it's pretty bad and I'd avoid doing anything important. By the way, unfortunate laptop can't be charged over USB-C, so you will have to carry around the 200 watt power brick. The laptop weighs 4.6 pounds and with the charger another 1.4. Manufacturers, please give us the option of USB-C charging for these powerful devices. Yes, I won't be able to fully power the laptop for high-end tasks, but it provides a nice option to bring a lighter charger on days that I don't need that. Props to Razer for being one of the few manufacturers to do this. The keyboard feels amazing to use, best keyboard I've used in a long time, and better than the arrows, spacious, ample key travel and the right tactile feel. Keys are backlit in zones, including secondary functions. I do like how there is these little lights that come on when certain modes are enabled, like when the volume is muted. Super helpful. The only issue is the placement of the delete key. There is a pause key where it would normally be. This calls me to make a very small number of typing errors. The trackpad is decent and works well enough, but it isn't one of the better ones I've used as it's not that smooth. The audio from the speakers comes out the side of the laptop and they don't get that loud, but I never found myself struggling to hear anything and the quality is good enough. It's no MacBook Pro 16, but all in all it's very usable. I really didn't do extensive battery tests, but I was getting about four hours with the screen slightly dimmed while writing this review. This kind of makes sense as the battery isn't the largest at 69 watt hours. Please note, if you unplug the power, the screen dims and calms become a little flora. You can fix this by turning off very bright in the AMD Radiant software. On battery, in performance mode the laptop was throttle to 20 watts of power running at 2.6 gigahertz. However, on occasion when I just pulled out the power cable and it switched to windows better battery mode, I saw the CPU hitting 3.9 gigahertz on all cores, so there must be a way to run it at full power. Lastly, price. I bought mine for $1,050 for the 8 gig model with 512 gig SSD, and $1,150 for the 16 gig model with one terabyte. I actually paid a bit more, but best by head one of their regular rotating sales the following week, and I called them and they priced matched, which was great. If you don't see these laptops for the price I paid, don't get frustrated. As mentioned, best by head rotating sales, be patient and it's likely they will go on sale again. Alright, let's wrap up. This laptop ended up being perfect for me. I was planning to get a higher end laptop with a 4k screen and add a second monitor for fast refresh rate gaming. I thought I'd have to settle for an Intel laptop and have to spend around $3,500. Instead, I got a laptop with a fast refresh rate screen, which was actually awesome as I can just use my current 4k monitor when I need to edit videos. It's insanely powerful, it runs cool and quiet, and I love the display. Including the upgrade to 32 gigahertz RAM and an additional 2 terabytes of storage, the whole thing cost me $1,650 USD. And bonus, it's smaller and lighter than the laptops I was looking at. Yes, there are some niggling issues that I highlighted in this review, but nothing that I'm worried about, especially for the price I paid. If I discover any solutions to the ones I've raised in this video, I'll post them in the description below. Look, before I go, I just want to say this, it's a bit of an end of an era. A year ago, this channel had a couple of 100 subscribers, now over 75,000 when I made this video. This will be the last time that you see me in this apartment as I'm moving to a new place, which will have a dedicated YouTube studio. Thank you for being on this journey with me, I appreciate it. If you like this video, you know what to do, smash that subscribe button, hit the thumbs up and the notification bell. And if you would like to support the channel even more, become a Patreon member. Until next time, I will catch you later.

The model I have here has the Ryzen 74750U processor with 8 cores and 16 threads, 16GB RAM and a 5.12GB SSD. Let's get straight into performance. In Geekbench, we see that this laptop is best in class. Why above Intel-based laptops for multi-core, including the new 10th-gen MacBook Pro, the Dell XPS 13 9300 and the ThinPad X-1 carbon? Turning to Cinebench R20, which maxes out the CPU, it was a thrashing with this laptop annihilating the competition, with the exception of my iD-Pad 514, which has a similar CPU. However, that laptop has an 8 core 8 thread processor, where this one has a 16 thread processor, so I would have expected it to beat out the iD-Pad 514 as well. I did question whether CPU temperatures are preventing it running faster, but when we look at them, they are superb. My CPU maxed out at 78 Celsius, way cooler than Intel-based CPUs, which often hit close to 100. So from that perspective, you probably don't need to get the T14 model with two fans, rather than this lighter T14S, as its single fan is able to call the CPU. When we turn to look at PowerDraw, we can see why this processor with its extra 8 threads doesn't beat the 4700U in the iD-Pad 514. It draws less power. This is actually a good thing, in my opinion. The performance is already phenomenal on this machine, and lower power draw results in less heat and increased battery life, which we'll talk about later. Chassis temperatures on the palm rest and keyboard deck are always nice and cool. That being said, it does get very warm towards the right side of the laptop. The exhaust vent for the fan is there. I prefer laptops that exhaust hot air out the back, not the side. I find laptops with this cooling design are more noticeably warm as the exhaust is closer to you. But, although the warmth of this chassis in this area is definitely noticeable, I didn't find it uncomfortable, and I am sensitive to this. Fan noise isn't the best. When underlight loads, the fans always run, but they are barely audible. When under heavy load, the fans don't get overly loud, however, they are high pitched, which makes them quite noticeable in a quiet room. For lightweight tasks though, like using Microsoft Office, the laptop is quiet enough. I didn't notice any coil wine in my unit. The laptop comes with a decently fast SSD, and RAM is in dual channel mode, which is good. It also comes with WiFi 6. When it comes to video editing in Premiere Pro, just like all Ryzen laptops without dedicated graphics, it's way too slow. Tons of people have mentioned that Premiere Pro has been optimized to work on AMD chips. Let me tell you that is Hogs Wallop. I have the latest version with the latest AMD drivers installed, and as of this video, in August 2020, it has not. I heard that DaVinci Resolve may run better on Ryzen's integrated graphics, so get subbed as I plan to give that a try in future videos. Audio latency is excellent, by the way, for those who need to know that. I had a really good time playing League of Legends on my laptop, it hit 120 frames per second on high graphics at 1920 resolution, which is very good. That being said, this laptop will not be able to handle AAA titles. Its internal graphics are just not powerful enough for that. So for casual gamers, this has you well covered, but serious gamers, this isn't your laptop. The display on my model is a 300-nit full HD panel with poor colour reproduction. That being said, you can configure it with higher end panels, including a 400-nit and 500-nit white. I do wish I had one of the higher end panels to test to see if their colours are any better, but I don't, unfortunately. I also wish they offered it with a 2K resolution panel. Not 4K, we don't need 4K in a laptop this size, but 2K would have made the fonts nice and crisp. Anyway, the display had no dead pixels or backlight bleed, which is good. The display is also a touch screen and has a matte panel, which I like, because it's not reflective, it helps make the most of the 300-nits of brightness and is usable in a brightly-lit room. This is a quality-feeling laptop, but not at the level of Apple's MacBook Pro. The large bezels though do make this laptop look very dated. That being said, when you're using it, you don't tend to notice them. The laptop can't be opened with one hand, which I found out the hard way. There are no sharp edges, and the back of the laptop is very easy to open with only 5 screws. Unfortunately, the RAM is soldered, but the SSD can be upgraded. In terms of chassis size, here it is compared to the incredible iD-Pad 515 and the Dell XPS 13 9300. The port choices are pretty good, 2 USB-C and 2 USB-A. Unfortunately, no thunderbolt on these AMD laptops though, which is a pity, because a laptop like this with a very powerful CPU could gain a lot by adding an external graphics card for those wanting to do video editing or gaming. The trackpad is great on this laptop, very accurate. It seems bigger than the one on the X1 Carbon, which I found a little cramped, so that is a plus. The keyboard is phenomenal. It's hard to verbalize how good it is. If Apple owns a trackpad category, the iPad's own the keyboard category. That being said, I don't like Lenovo's default layout, where the function of control key is swapped. However, you can easily swap them in the BIOS. Speakers are really good for a laptop like this. They get very loud. That being said, they don't have much bass. Plus, they are downward facing, so you'll lose some volume if you want to. That being said, the volume gets so loud that I don't see even that being an issue. Battery life and performance while on battery is just awesome. It really does make the most of its 57 watt-hour battery. I've seen 10 plus hours remaining even after I've used 20% of the battery. Sorry that I didn't take a shot at that, but here is another example. As I discussed earlier, this Ryzen CPU just doesn't draw a lot of power, which is probably a major contributor to its great battery life. I wish I knew how long the battery life is on the upgraded model with the 400-net low power screen. By default, if you unplug the power cable, the screen's brightness stems to 100 nits, and the performance slider in Windows shifts to battery mode, capping the CPU's performance at 1.4GHz drawing a max of 10 watts. But, and this is pretty cool. You can change the performance slider back to best performance to get the full processing power while on battery, which is pretty rare for PC laptops. Please note, by default, you won't be able to raise the brightness back from 100 nits after I'm plugging it, even if you plug it back in. This can easily be solved by opening the AMD Radeon software and turning off the battery bright. Once I restarted the computer, this issue went away. The laptop does support both Windows hello and my unit has a fingerprint reader as well. The webcam is the usual awful one. However, better quality webcam for it just came out in the new iMac 27 for 2020 will hopefully make their way better. Mine did have a privacy filter though, which is good. The laptop was very stable in my testing and didn't crash once. I do like the Lenovo offers a range of options to add extended warranties, including nest-day, onset servicing in many locations and accident protection. Price-wise, Lenovo's website can be tough here. Prices seem to fluctuate frequently, with heavy discounts often coming out. and didn't crash once. I do like the Lenovo offers a range of options to add extended warranties, including next-day onsite servicing in many locations and accident protection. At the time I made this video, the 6 core 12th road model with 8GB RAM, 256GB SSD, and a 300-nits screen goes for about 1,250. It is nice to see an option to upgrade to 32GB RAM, especially as the RAM is soldered, but it is pricey compared to what one would have been able to purchase it for if it was user-appgradable. So enough said, who is this laptop for and would I personally buy it? So far, this is a rather unique laptop. It's the first portable somewhat premium Ryzen 4000 laptop that I've tested, and this means that this laptop doesn't suffer from any of the major drawbacks of other Ryzen 4000 laptops that I've used. For example, the Redmi book, Laksa webcam, and Backlit Keyboard. The Aces ZenBook, you can't make out the Backlit Keyboard on their light coloured models. The main drawback is it doesn't have options for a higher resolution more colour accurate panel, like the Max phenomenal retina display or the Spectre's OLED display. With that in mind, I feel this laptop is a really good option for casual users and programmers who don't mind a full HD screen rather than a higher resolution one. In fact, I'm going to go as far as saying right now it's an excellent option for programmers. It's insanely powerful, has the best keyboard. titulo: The Budget Laptop for Creators & Gamers - Asus Zenbook 14 - (Ryzen 4500U + NVIDIA MX350) @$550
transcricao: Tech Family, the moment I saw this laptop with its combination of the new Ryzen 4500 new processor added in video MX 350 graphics for $550 I knew I had to try. Seriously, I've been wanting to see how potent a new Ryzen processor with a dedicated Nvidia graphics card would be in a budget laptop for some time. Plus, I've been wanting to see how ASUS' budget laptop stack up with my current favorite, the incredibly popular IdeaPad 5. Look, I value your time, so I'm just going to get down to it. I really like this laptop. It is the best option I've seen for video editing on a budget, and today I'm going to show you why. I'm also going to tell you why I still prefer the IdeaPad 515 for casual users and coders. By the way, I'm Josh, and I buy and review a lot of laptops and talk tech from the perspective of what it's like to own and use these devices. If at the end of this video, you like what you watched, make sure to smash that subscribe button, click the thumbs up and the notification bell. It shows your appreciation for the incredible amount of work that goes into making these. Just a quick note here, this isn't going to be as in-depth as I normally go in my reviews, as I wanted to rush a video out for you because there is just so much exciting stuff to cover about it. If this video does become popular though, I'll probably do a follow-up review. Anyway, let's start with performance. The Ryzen 4500U is already a very capable processor, and for CPU-related tasks, this laptop performs similar to the IdeaPad 515 Geekbench. However, in Synabench, which maxes out the CPU, it performs a bit worse, but it's still in the same ballpark. The good news here is it runs quieter. In fact, its fan is hardly ever audible in light use, and even when running the Synabench benchmark or exporting a 4K video from Premiere Pro, it was very quiet. It's definitely quieter for light usage than the IdeaPad 5, both the 14 and 15-inch versions. That being said, it does get warmer to the touch than those laptops, but nothing uncomfortable like the furnace known as the Dell XPS 9300. Back to the performance results, and take a look how this laptop beats that far more expensive Dell XPS 9300, as well as the new 10th gen equipped MacBook Pros. But what I was most eager to see is how much the included Nvidia MX350 graphics boosted performance. Even though the MX350 is not that powerful, it beat the internal graphics of Ryzen by almost 50% in both Geekbench's graphics test as well as Fire Strikes, so definitely worth it. Where it really helped, though, was in Premiere Pro doing a standard 4K H.264 export, which is a very common task for YouTubers like me. You can see here just how much faster this laptop is than the IdeaPad 5 15 without that dedicated graphics. Now some folks will say that this is a Premiere problem, and it's not optimized for Ryzen's internal graphics. This may be true, however, that is a benefit of having Nvidia's graphics. More programs are optimized for Nvidia's CUDA when it comes to rendering and encoding, because it's been out a longer time. So, moral of the story is this. This laptop is a better all-round performer than other laptops with only an AMD Ryzen USB-U. Oh, and take a peek at how this little $550 laptop destroys expensive laptops with Intel's Tension CPU and their new G7 graphics on that same test. Moving along, the next major thing I like about this laptop is the display. It is far more color accurate than the display is in my IdeaPad's. It's a step above and you really do notice the difference. In fact, this is the only laptop I've ever seen at this price range with such a color accurate display. This with a combination of the dedicated graphics means that this is the only laptop I'd consider for photo or video editing so far in the sub $800 USD price range. By the way, the display has very good viewing angles. However, my unit unfortunately had a decent amount of backlight bleed. Unlike my IdeaPad 515 which came with a touchscreen, this ASUS N-Book 14 did not. The laptop has ample ports including HDMI, USB-C, 3USBA and a microSD card reader. What's great is the USB ports are all the faster USB 3.1 Gen 2. Normally, I'd only seen Gen 1 in this price range. The keyboard is comfortable to use with good key travel. Amazing! How ASUS can put a comfortable keyboard in their laptop but Apple can't do it with their non-magic keyboards in their latest MacBook Pros, which cost more than double. The laptop comes with 8GB of RAM in dual-channel mode which is good. It also comes with WiFi 6. Apple, again, seriously. How can this little cheap laptop have WiFi 6 but your MacBook Pro 13 for 2020 card? It does open with one hand and comes with Windows Hello facial recognition. On that note, the back of the laptop does lift off the table when you open it for increased airflow which is good. I was concerned the edge of the bottom of the screen would cut into my leg and be uncomfortable on my lap. I was pleasantly surprised that it wasn't at all. The weight of the laptop is excellent. It's super portable at 2.5 lbs or 1.15kg and the form factor of this laptop is very compact. Here it is next to my iDepad 514. Battery life is good. I was getting around 6 hours doing word processing with the screen at max brightness. It's a little smaller than the iDepad 515's battery at 50 watts compared to 57. Lastly, the price of this laptop is just stupid. I bought mine on a July 4th sale for $550 which is epic. So that's a lot of pros right. Let's get into the cons. This laptop can't be charged by the USB-C port. This is really frustrating in 2020. Charging by the USB-C port is just so convenient as there's so many devices converging on that standard so you'll find plenty of those charges available. I have seen some, USB-C to barrel pin charger converters available on Amazon that supposedly will enable you to charge off a USB-C power adapter but I haven't tried any so can't speak to their reliability. What elevates this issue is that the adapter the laptop comes with is very short so you'll probably be using it in combination with an extension cord. The keyboard, although comfortable to type on, has some negatives. It's very hard to see the keys in many lighting conditions because the key color is white on silver which doesn't offer a lot of contrast between the colors. Plus the backlight is not very strong at all. Heck, even in daylight the shadow caused by the screen on the secondary function keys makes them hard to read. Also, and importantly, the placement of the function key on the right side is where you'd expect the right arrow key to be which causes me to sometimes miss hitter. The trackpad is a little too slippery for my liking and I found myself struggling to be accurate with it even though it uses the Windows precision drivers. Honestly, the keyboard and trackpad on the iDepad 515 is just better. Normally I write these reviews on the device I'm reviewing but in this case I switched mid-scrept to complete it on the iDepad 515 as I just infine this laptop as comfortable. The next thing is that the build quality of the laptop is pretty good for a plastic laptop but it just isn't on the same level as the iDepad 515 and 14. Although as I mentioned, the performance is very good in this laptop. One part that is a letdown is the SSD speeds. This is one of the slowest SSDs I've seen in a laptop in a very long time. That being said, I really don't think it will affect most people who will buy this laptop but I still felt it worth me calling out. The sound gets surprisingly loud which is good but but but but the bass is just not there at all. It's like listening to music where there is only mid-range and treble playing. Also, the speakers are downward facing so expect a lot less volume when using this laptop on your lap. Like the Redmi book, I struggled to get the back off the laptop as there are two screws underneath the rubber feet that I couldn't get out without ripping them off the laptop which I don't want to do. Even so, I did some research and it seems the RAM is soldered and not use it upgradable but that's the same as the iDepads. Compared to the similar priced iDepad 515, you are losing out on that bigger screen and the 512GB faster SSD. Lastly, I did find on several occasions when I closed the lid the laptop did not go correctly understand by and it became very warm in my backpack. I thought that sort of thing was the thing of the past. Folks, I need to update you on two issues that appeared late in the review. Although Premiere Pro exported correctly and fast the first time on additional exports I did get this error you see on screen, both in Premiere Pro and also Media and Coda. Two, the sound stopped working both from the speakers and headphones. As you can see here I'm playing one of my YouTube videos and you can't hear anything even though the audio is up. It's weird as it was originally working. I did update all the drivers and buys etc callacess tech support and they couldn't fix the issue so I will be returning mine to Best Buy. I did search the net including Reddit and other reviews and no one else is reporting this so I assume it's just my unit. But if you do buy this laptop make sure to test it thoroughly to ensure it's working well and I have a video on how to do that which I'll post in the description below. So let's wrap up. If your budget is up to $700 US dollars and you do photo, video editing or want a better gaming experience this Acesenbook 14 is the number one laptop I would recommend for you. And for heaven's sake don't let what happened to the iDipad 515 inch happen here. Buy it before it sells out. If you're planning to focus on computer coding though or office work I would go with the iDipad 515 it's a more comfortable device to use. The keyboard is better, the trackpad is more accurate, it has USB-C charging and the bigger 15 inch screen is just more luxurious for productivity work. Plus that laptop is crazy lightweight and portable anyway even for a 15 inch. Well that's all for today folks if you like this video you know what to do. Smash that subscribe button, click the thumbs up and then notification bell until next time I will catch you later.

titulo: RedmiBook 16 - The AMAZING Laptop!! ... with a couple of gotchas
transcricao: Tech Family, we have been waiting for one of the new 8 core Ryzen 4000 series processors coupled with a great screen in a high and chassis for under a thousand US dollars. Today, that search may be over. With me is the Redmi Book 16 with the Ryzen 4700U processor, 16 gigabram and a 512GB SSD, a super promising device by the Chinese manufacturer Xiaomi. Hopefully I didn't watch the pronunciation with my Australian accent, like I seem to have so many things, but I'm sure you'll correct me if I do in the comments below. Speaking of comments, I've had a tiny number of people post in prior videos saying they won't buy from a Chinese manufacturer. This channel is about promoting and celebrating innovation, wherever it may be. I will continue to delete such nonsense comments. Plus, most American manufacturers source their parts and assembly from China anyway. So I really don't know what these people are talking about. I'm Josh and I buy and review a lot of laptops and talk tech from the perspective of what it's like to actually own and use the devices. If after watching, you like what you saw, don't forget to smash that subscribe button, hit the thumbs up and the notification bell. It shows your appreciation for the incredible amount of work that goes into making these. I'm going to do this review a little differently as it's such a unique laptop. I'm first going to walk you through the incredible pros and then go over some pretty concerning cons. Finally, I'll wrap up by covering who should buy this machine. Let's get into it. The first pro is the chassis. It looks and feels like such a premium device. It's definitely a step up in build quality from other devices in this price range. That being said, don't expect Apple levels of build quality here. It's just not there. The screen does open with one hand and importantly, it looks nice and clean out of the box with only one sticker. The bezels are very small on this 16 inch laptop. It's a little wider than the MacBook Pro 16, but not as tall. Not because this is a 16 by 9 inch screen rather than the MacBook Pro 16 by 10. Honestly, though, on a screen is large, there is plenty of real estate even vertically. It's lighter than the MacBook Pro 16, which is incredible as that laptop is already very light. It's just a tad heavier than the iDF had 515. The next pro, and it is a big one, is fan noise. I'm delighted to report that this is one of the quietest laptops I've ever used. Seriously guys, it is silent for light to medium tasks most of the time and it is quieter than the two iDF pads I've tested, even though those weren't overly loud to begin with. Only under full load do you start to hear the fans, and even then it is far from the loudest laptop I've tested. Another massive pro is heat that you would actually feel on a chassis. I am blown away by how cool this chassis feels, both on the keyboard deck and underside when on my lap. It is substantially cool to the touch when under load than any other laptop I've ever tested. I seriously was questioning whether I had a faulty heat gun when I was testing it, but just by touching a laptop you can feel how cool it runs. I guess it's a combination of putting one of these new Ryzen CPUs in a decent sized well-cooled chassis. Next is the display. It is a very good one and one of the best full HD screens I've tested to date. You can see how colour accurate it is on screen. It is a significant step up from the iDF had 5, 14, 15 and the Swift 3. And it even competes with the MacBook Air's colour accuracy. Also, don't let the brightness of only 300 nits to tow you too much. On a large 16-inch matte panel, which does not have any reflections, 300 nits of brightness is good enough to see in a bright little room. Also, I personally was expecting that the full HD 1920x1080 pixels stretched over a large 16-inch screen would result in me seeing actual pixels due to the lower pixel density. I am pleased to say that this wasn't an issue for me. And it has opened my mind to 17-inch 1920x1080 gaming displays that I would have previously avoided. The screen is not a touch screen, my unit arrived with no dead pixels and I didn't notice any PWM flickering to lower the brightness. The only downside was it did have some backlight bleeding. Overall, this is the first screen that I found in the sub-$1,000 price range that is good enough for some photo and video editing. Performance is another pro of this laptop, it is an absolute beast. It performs very well in benchmarks like Geekbench, destroying far more expensive competitors like the MacBook Pro 13. The same can be said about Synomenche R20 as well. Obviously a lot of this is due to the new Ryzen CPU in this well-called laptop. I mean check out the max CPU temperatures in this Synomenche R20 run. It's in the mid-70s Celsius. That is insanely cool for an 8-core processor. In my MacBook Pro 16, with its Intel 8-core processor, you'd see it in the 90s. This laptop, 16GB of RAM, runs at 2666 MHz and is configured in dual-channel, which is good. The SSD performance though is very poor. I believe it's equipped with an older SATA 3 SSD. That being said for the most part, it doesn't seem to affect real-world application performance. Laptop startup time was decent. Opening a word document was very fast. Programming tasks were also fast, including starting the integrated development environment in Telage A, doing a code compile followed by running the code on the J-BOSS application server in debug mode. The only task that was on the slower side was reloading a large MySQL database, which is a mostly single threaded task and therefore doesn't benefit from the 8 cores. This could also be hindered by the slower SSD. When your latency wasn't great, although be aware I did run some heavy tasks to push the laptop while this test was running. Wi-Fi speeds were also excellent, although I do not believe this has Wi-Fi 6. I did play a couple of rounds of League of Legends on higher settings at 1920 by 1080 and found it very playable getting around 90 frames per second. I do think that this laptop is good enough to play light games at 1080 resolution on medium settings, but look elsewhere if you want to play AAA titles. Another pro is that this laptop has a decent selection of ports. There are USB-A ports on both sides of the laptop which is convenient and two USB-C ports on the left side that both support charging. Also, the ports are super stiff to plug into and feel very high quality. I had no issues operating an external 4K monitor over display port using the USB-C connection running at 60Hz for the full resolution. By the way, I did have to install the adrenaline driver from AMD to get this working. Prior to installing the driver, the laptop did not recognize it was plugged into an external monitor via either USB-C or HDMI. The keyboard feels very good to type on with decent space in key travel. Honestly, it felt better than Apple's supposed magic keyboards. Mine came in English which was a relief as this is a Chinese laptop and the layout was very standard which is also good. The trackpad was excellent, very smooth glide and Windows precision accuracy. It felt better than the new Dell XPS laptops. Battery life was also good which surprised me as it only has a 46 watt hour battery. I was getting about 6 hours of light use on full brightness with Windows performance mode set to better performance. I feel like it would be able to push maybe 8 hours if you lower the brightness settings and the performance mode. The charger is also crazy small and lightweight for a 65 watt one, making the whole package feel extremely portable. By the way, it did come with some really odd extras in the box, including an international to American power converter which you don't need as the charger is already an American one, plus it came with a USB-A to micro USB cable, no idea why. Lastly, the price is excellent. At 920 USD which is the total amount I paid on Gearbest all set and done, a site that sells Chinese products internationally. So that's a lot of pros right. Before you go running out to buy one, let's go through the rather significant cons. The first one which is a pretty big one is that this laptop only comes with a Chinese language Windows license. That means that it will not let you switch to English in Windows and even if you try to reinstall a fresh copy of the English version of Windows, the product key that this laptop comes with will not be accepted. Yep, you have to purchase a new Windows key, currently $139 USD for the home version. Luckily for me, I had an unused license that I had purchased to run my Mac in boot camp, but that does take the cost of this laptop up significantly from about $900 USD to around $1,050 USD. Now the laptop does not come with a webcam at all, which may be a showstopper for those who spend their days on Zoom. Any equality, while very good, doesn't get that loud, and the speakers are placed on the bottom of the laptop, so they will become muffled if you use the laptop on your laptop, say on a blanket or sitting up in bed. Take a listen. I don't believe the keyboard is backlit, at least I couldn't find any way to turn on a backlight. So using it at night in a dark room will be challenging. Also, even though the chassis felt very premium, I did find the edges felt reasonably sharp at some angles. I found the back of the laptop very hard to open up to get at the internals. Even though screws are exposed, I believe there is one screw under one of the back rubber feet that I couldn't get to. As this is such a nice laptop, I didn't want to push this too hard, so that's why you aren't seeing any footage of the internals here. Let me know if you really want to see the internals in the comments below, and I may rethink this. Next, the ports. Even though plentiful, they are slow. Seriously, one of these USB-A ports is USB 2.0, which is 480 Mbps, I mean nowadays modern ports start at a minimum of 5 Gbps. Plus, it would have been nice to have an SD card reader, and because both of the charging ports are on the left side, you will have to run a cable around the back if your power outlet is on the right. This is annoying, especially as the power cable it comes with is very short. There is also no way to quickly log into the laptop with a fingerprint reader or Windows Hello facial recognition. It's odd, as the advertising material said it had some sort of smart sensor key, which I'm assuming meant a fingerprint logging. If there is, I certainly couldn't find it in my install. Also minor thing, the laptop arrived in the most ludicrous packaging. I originally wanted to do an unboxing for you all to some nice B-roll music, but couldn't because it was crazy hard to get into. It was literally covered in packaging tape. And lastly, but importantly, if you have any issues with this laptop, you will have to ship it back to China, which may substantially delay the time it takes to get your machine replaced or fixed. Plus, after a bit of research into retailer gear best, it seems they will only pay for return shipping if it is dead on arrival. So if you decide you don't want the laptop and want a return, expect it expensive charge to send it back to China. So where does this leave us? Overall, this is a very comfortable laptop to use, as Yamigets the basics right. It's very lightweight, it has a big color accurate screen, it's got an excellent keyboard and trackpad, almost no fan noise, and it doesn't get warm to the touch at all. But I personally can't recommend it for most people, especially non-Chinese buyers who will have a tougher time getting support and have to buy their own Windows key. For most people shopping in this price range, I think the Lenovo X1 Carbon 7th gen or the Slim 7th Ryzen, which I'm yet to test, are much better all-round choices. Yes, they will have downsides compared to this laptop, but I think they are better for most people. I'd only recommend this laptop for someone who absolutely wants a silent and core running laptop for around $1000 with a big screen and powerful components above all else, and is therefore truly okay with the downsides like no webcam or a backlit keyboard. Anyway folks, that's all for today. If you liked this video, you know what to do. Smash that subscribe button, hit the thumbs up and the notification bell. Until next time, I will catch you later.

titulo: Lenovo X1 Carbon 8th Gen Review - Getting The Basics RIGHT!
transcricao: Tech Family, with me is the new Lenovo X1 Carbon 8th generation. I value your time, so I'm just going to cut to the chase and tell you that this is an almost pointless refresh as it is essentially the same laptop as the 7th generation. That being said, whether 7th or 8th generation, this laptop is still excellent. It's one of the very rare ones that get to the basics right and has many advantages over competitors including the new Dell XPS, the MacBook Air for 2020 and even the MacBook Pro 13. Plus, by relaunching it as the 8th generation, the Lenovo has given us a nice side effect that the supposed older 7th generation will probably be cheaper. I'm Josh and I buy and review a lot of laptops and talk tech from the perspective of what it's like to actually own and use these devices. If at the end of this video you like what you watched, make sure to smash that subscribe button, hit the thumbs up and the notification bell, it shows your appreciation for the incredible amount of work that normally goes into making these. Although in this case, Lenovo's made my job easier by effectively rebranding the same laptop as I already reviewed. On that note, this is going to be a rather brief video as so little has changed from the 7th generation. If you haven't watched my review of that laptop yet, please do so as this one is meant to build on that. I'm going to place a link to it in the description below. And by the way, this laptop was said to me by Lenovo there were no strings attached, they gave me no direction in what I'm to say and they haven't reviewed this video before I posted it, which is good because I wouldn't have accepted the review unit if there were. Alright, so pretty much nothing material has changed in this 8th generation. It does have a better looking top cover which in my opinion looks much cleaner than the previous carbon fiber we. It has new function buttons but picking up and hanging up calls which I probably won't use, Wi-Fi 6 which you can upgrade easily and cheaply anyway, and the Intel 10th gen processors which were already available in the 7th generation X1 carbon. By the way, it is rather annoying that both Lenovo and Intel refers to their product lines as generations because it means I keep having to clarify that this laptop is the 8th generation while the processor inside it is the 10th generation. Anyway, please note that these aren't the newer iSlate processors with the faster G7 graphics that you'll find in the new Dell XPS9300 or the MacBook Pro 13 for 2020. These are from Comat Lake which uses the older 14 nanometer process but we'll see how it performs in a second. Also, they removed the option for the 6th generation X4 processor that last year's model had which I'm kind of okay with as this really isn't the machine for people looking for a lot of power. You can see on the screen my performance results are around the same as the prior model with the only increase likely due to my review unit coming with the 10310u CPU which has a slightly faster turbo boost speed than the model I owned before. They are both well below the MacBook Pro 13 for 2020 and a bit below the Dell XPS9300 which both have the newer iSlate processors. That being said, it does perform substantially better than the quad core MacBook Air for 2020. While watching how the CPU responds under load, I could see that it quickly hits 4.4GHz which is the max turbo for this processor while drawing a whopping 45 watts of power. After a couple of seconds it drops to 35 watts and then stabilizes at around 2.9GHz drawing 27 watts of power. During this the CPU temperatures max out at 98 Celsius and yes the laptop does come with a 65 watt charger so it won't rain the battery during these high wattage bursts. In terms of temperatures that you would actually feel, this is where this laptop really starts to shine. It runs very cool to the touch. In terms of fan noise, for most tasks I did on the laptop it was silent. In fact this is one of the quietest laptops I have ever used. When under load it is similar to the Dell XPS9300 which isn't too bad. You will hear the fans but they aren't as loud as something like the MacBook Pro 13 for 2020. Somehow quiet it normally is, you will notice the fans spin up on occasion when it's processing something. That being said it is nowhere near as disturbing as the MacBook Air for 2020 which can suddenly run its fans very loud. The SSD is a good amount faster in this year's model but obviously that is not a reason to consider it over the older one especially as you can upgrade it anyway. On my 7th generation I bought the 4K screen but as mentioned in my review it had really bad PWM flickering when you lower the brightness leading me to recommend viewers get the 1080 panel instead. I'm glad to report that my recommendation was sound as this display really has no noticeable problems with PWM. As you can see the panel has good enough brightness and calibrary production. It's better than the cheaper iDLE pad slightly worse than the MacBook Air and definitely not as good as the MacBook Pro and the Dell XPS. That being said I am comparing this display to the higher resolution retina and more expensive 4K displays in those laptops which isn't really fair. However as mentioned I did try the X1 carbons 4K screen but PWM made it unusable. And note I actually had two of the same laptops with this screen, one had some backlight bleed and the other didn't. At night make sure to check that yours is good and exchange it if not. Anyway this is the kind of screen that is definitely good enough for office work, movie watching, browsing the web and coding. However it is not a screen that I would recommend for anyone doing photo or video editing. So let's cut the crap. This laptop is basically the same as last year's model. So why am I reviewing it? Well for starters, after reviewing so many laptops and now we are using what effectively is the same X1 carbons 7 generation that I reviewed several months ago, I realized that this is one of the very rare laptops that just gets the important things right without major issues. The keyboard is so comfortable to use. They are coupled with the fact that it is insanely lightweight at 2.4lbs, it runs mostly silent, it doesn't get warm to the touch and it's much faster than the similar price MacBook Air plus it has USB-A ports just makes it a very comfortable convenient laptop to use. For its intended use the only thing I really don't like about it are one, the placement of the page up and down keys which I sometimes accidentally press, two, the fact that all the charging ports are on the left side so if my power outlets on the right side I have to run a cable around the back, and three, for some reason I can't swap the odd loud of the function and control key to a normal via Lenovo's Vantage software like I used to be able to on the 7th generation. I now have to do it in the BIOS. But guys, I'm really just nitpicking here. A nice side effect of Lenovo coming out with this 8-gen model is that it will likely make the supposed older 7-gen model cheaper, even though we know it's basically the same thing. The 7-gen of this laptop really feels a gap in the $1,000 to $1,300 price range for casual users or those doing lightweight programming such as students, and be on the lookout for deals. I'd strongly recommend you consider it over the 2020 MacBook Air as it has a better keyboard, it's lighter, and it's got a proper cooling solution, which means it runs faster and quieter. What the MacBook Air has over this laptop is its base model comes with a higher resolution panel and a little bit better battery life, but that being said, this battery in here is pretty decent anyway. If you are considering the XPS 139300, I definitely recommend you get this over that laptop as that one just runs way too hot to the touch. Well that was a quick review for today, but stay tuned as I have some surprises coming. Anyway. In this video, you know what to do, smash that subscribe button, hit the thumbs up, and the notification bell until next time, I'll catch you later.

titulo: Surface Laptop 3 Review (AMD)
transcricao: Okay Tech Family, quick video here. Originally I wasn't planning to review the Surface Laptop 3 as it has already been widely reviewed. But I got it as a present for my mother and we'll use it over the last couple of days out of curiosity. I noticed a couple of issues that I haven't seen others cover, one of which I would consider quite serious. By the way, the model I have here is the AMD Ryzen 716 Gigafram 512GB SSD version. This is going to be a brief, purely qualitative review with my thoughts on this laptop. Firstly, as I mentioned, I want to want perspective buyers about an issue that I haven't seen anyone else cover in detail. The speakers come from below the keyboard deck and when listening to vocals there is substantial audible buzzing or rattling when the volume is above about 30%. The louder the volume, the louder the buzzing. This makes this laptop impossible to use for comment tasks like watching Netflix or videos like this on YouTube. A quick search on the internet revealed that this issue was widely reported by many other owners, so I am not alone. As mentioned, I was hoping to give this laptop to my mother, but I considered this a completely show stopping issue for most users. Secondly, I have had lockups and lag using this laptop. Sometimes when I try to change the display brightness using the function keys, they simply don't work. Check this out for an issue. I am going to raise the display brightness here using the settings with the mouse. You can see me raising the brightness. Then I am going to press display brightness up here on the keyboard to raise it a little bit more. Bam, it drops back down. It is completely frozen, so I am moving the mouse. Nothing is happening, okay? The mouse is kind of stuck up here. You can see up here. Other times when moving the mouse, there is lag. Yes, I have installed the latest version of Windows, Drivers, etc. And yes, I have checked the internet as to whether others are also reporting this. And they are. Thirdly, the screen for a higher resolution display is surprisingly dull and lacks contrast compared to others in this category. Let me give you a real world example of why this sucks. I normally like to run my laptops to show more information on the screen by pulling the scaling below the recommended value. In this case, changing it from 150% scaling to 125% scaling. Unfortunately, as the resolution on this laptop isn't the highest, this change is a big jump in how much smaller text and icons become when I change this setting. Normally on high resolution displays, I have more flexibility here. Fan noise. Normally this is pretty good, but I have noticed that when the laptop is plugged into an external monitor, at times the fans can run very loud. And lastly, this laptop is stupidly expensive. At a decent spec with 16gb RAM and 512gb storage, you are looking at a price of $2,100, which is knocking on the door of the MacBook Pro 16 base model. That laptop has the same amount of RAM, SSD, but includes 6 core processor, better graphics, and to be honest, is a far superior machine. Let me cut to the point here. This is a beautiful looking light weight laptop that does have some positives, like a decent keyboard and a trackpad. But that's where it ends. Realistically, this is a pretty shell in casing an overpriced machine that has lacklaster performance and issues. If you are having a different experience with this laptop, don't hesitate to share your experiences in the comments below. If you like this video, you know what to do, smash that subscribe button, click the thumbs up and the notification bell. I would certainly appreciate it. Till next time, I'll catch you later.

titulo: Dell XPS 15 (9500) Review - Everything YOU Need To Know!!
transcricao: Tech Family, get A! With me as the new Dell XPS 9500-15-inch, I absolutely love this laptop and through this review I'm going to tell you why, but I'm also going to tell you why I'll be returning it. I'm Josh and I ban review a lot of laptops and unfortunately in Dell's case return a lot of them. If after watching this video you like what you watched, make sure to smash that subscribe button, hit the thumbs up and the notification bell, it shows your appreciation for the incredible amount of hours that goes into making these. Alright, the model that I have here is the 10758 model from Intel's 10th generation line with 6 cores and 12 threads. It has 16 giga-gram, a 1TB SSD and a G41650 Ti. Normally I start off with performance but today let's start with the chassis instead, as it is completely redesigned for this year. Let me first say it looks stunning, solid construction all the way around, the edge to edge display just looks so elegant and modern, even compared to the MacBook Pro 16 which really is saying something, as the bezels on that laptop aren't that big to begin with. It's a good amount smaller than the MacBook Pro 16, however it actually weighs a tad more at 4.6 pounds first the MacBook Pro 16's 4.5. Yes, I know my laptops weigh a tad more than what the manufacturer's claimed but it is what it is. Because these laptops weigh a similar amount and both fit into a 15 inch laptop sleeve, I am going to draw comparisons between the two as they are in the same class of portability. A lot of people might be like no, you should only compare the MacBook Pro 16 to the new Dell XPS 17. That laptop for a similar spec is much heavier at 5.5 pounds and the chassis will not fit into a 15 inch laptop sleeve. Anyway, back to the 15, it feels quite dense to hold due to its size to weight ratio, the screen can be opened with one hand and I notice no sharp edges. The display is excellent, one of the best I've ever used, it actually has more pixels on a stand-in 4K at 3840x2400 due to its 16x10 aspect ratio. This aspect ratio is a dream for productivity work including using office applications and coding. I personally like it better than Microsoft's 3x2 aspect ratio on their laptops because it is also decent at playing movies as it doesn't force super big black borders above and below the movie. The brightness is insanely high which makes it a good laptop to use outdoors or in a bright environment. Even though the glass on the screen does pick up some reflections, the high brightness negates this. The display isn't quite as good as the MacBook Pro 16s in terms of color accuracy but it's still an excellent display. I noticed no dead pixels, no backlight bleeding and no PWM flickering used to lower the brightness. It's also a touchscreen which is a nice touch. The keyboard is quite good, large spacious keys, Apple key travel and a well-known keyboard layout with no keys in our places. That being said, I do find it feels quite mushy to type on. It doesn't quite reach the heights of the Surface Book or ThinkPad keyboards but I definitely found it better than Apple's Magic Keyboard. The trackpad is larger than previous years but there is a serious issue with it. It seems to be kind of loose where there are two clicks to it rather than one. It's like you press down and you pass click one and then you have to click down further for it to actually register. That means if you only pass click one it doesn't register the click. Take a look at this video of me trying to click into the drop down box on screen. You can hear it clicking but it doesn't register. What sucks is this isn't like Apple's trackpad where the trackpad doesn't move at all and the click is software based. This trackpad is mechanical and likely can't be fixed by a driver update. Now before anyone says I have a limit, no I do not. There are many early buyers on Reddit reporting this. Check out these threats. Due to this issue I had an unusually high amount of misclicks. It is annoying but I was able to make do after I got used to how to click on it. For over $2,000 US dollars I will return mine to see if I can get one without this issue. The port situation is almost perfect. It has a fast full size SD card reader. Yay! It also has three USB C ports, two of which are Thunderbolt and all support charging. I also like that there are USB C ports on each side for maximum flexibility of way to plug in. I just wish it had one USB A port. Let's take a look at performance. As per usual these tests were run all with the latest drivers, buyers and windows updates installed. The results were excellent. You can see that the new Intel 10th Gen 6 core chip performs better than the older 9th Gen by around 10%. It was only bested by the 9th Gen 8 core chip in the MacBook Pro 16 and might I say not by that much. Likely due to thermal limitations in the MacBook Pro 16. The 9th Gen 8 core chip in the Aero 17 beat it handly but that is a substantially bigger laptop with much better thermals. Taking a look at Cinebench R20 which maxes out the CPU, it's a similar picture. My only note here is pat on the back to the $750 Lenovo iDepad 514 with its Ryzen 4700 U for performing on par with this laptop. I recently crowded the Kina Budget laptops and results like this show why. I'll post a link to that video in the description below. When we look at power draw under load, you can see that this laptop initially starts by drawing 90 watts and then drops to 39 and slowly increases to 45. It's about as expected but again props to the Ryzen laptops. Take a look at how little powered the iDepad 514 used to achieve the same performance results as this laptop. Please, manufacturers start putting Ryzen CPUs in your high end laptops. Here are my CPU performance results and as you can see this laptop hit 4.1GHz max and then settle down at 3GHz when under load. Know when you're the claim 5GHz in the marketing. When running these tests the CPU temperatures sat close to 100 Celsius, often hitting that mark, similar to the smaller XPS 13. I did try all of Dell's performance modes and found little difference between them. Even when I undervolted the CPU by negative 100mV, the only exception being cool, which appeared to boost the fan speed while substantially dropping the power to the CPU. In real world performance the laptop performed extremely well. Starting the laptop and opening a word document were both very fast. I got excellent results in my coding tests as well, including starting the integrated development environment in Teluguay, compiling Java code, starting the J-boss application server in debug mode and reloading a large MySQL database. Premier Pro export times to the popular H.264 format were great as well. Gaming performance in this laptop was also excellent, given it isn't a gaming laptop. On screen are my 5 strike scores, as you can see this laptop scored almost 9000, which puts it well above the GTX 1650 in the MSI Prestige 15 and within striking distance of the GTX 1060 in the Alienware 13R3, which was the go-to laptop gaming graphics card for many years. Needless to say, it had no problems playing basic titles like League of Legends at way more than the screen 60 FPS on ultra settings at 1920x1200. In fact, I played a couple of rounds of the more intensive title Battlefield 1 with the settings on screen and got a solid 60 FPS in combat, which is very good. Let's talk about fan noise, when doing light towers such as browsing the web or using Microsoft Word you will hear the fans, especially if you're in a quiet room. They tend to come on for a while and then turn off, which actually makes them more noticeable since they have a higher pitch sound to them. By the way, as I mentioned earlier, I found that Dell's quiet mode didn't really do a lot here. That being said, under heavy load it's actually one of the quieter laptops I've tested maxing out at 43 decibels. One interesting thing with this laptop compared to others is if I lift it off the table while under heavy load, it really sounds like a jet engine. Somehow Dell have managed to keep the loud fan noise well constrained. Overall though, I am quite sensitive to fan noise and I didn't find this laptop that bad at all. These are under light loads and the MacBook Pro 13 and 16 which are mostly silent, but it isn't as loud as many laptops I've tested. It's probably fine to use in a classroom or a quiet library. By the way, I didn't notice any core wine in my unit. Chassis temperatures, the ones you would actually feel when using this laptop, for basic tasks the laptop gets a little warm when your hands are. It's noticeable but not overly distracting and again I'm sensitive to this sort of thing. When gaming, I did notice a significantly high temperature on the left side of the keyboard deck compared to the right. This felt a bit uncomfortable but nowhere near as uncomfortable as the Razer Blade 15, whose chassis temperatures get really hot when gaming. Under full CPU load though, this laptop did reach similar temperatures to the MacBook Pro 16 but didn't get as hot as the furnace known as the XPS 13 9300. SSD speeds were good and I'm happy to report substantially faster than the underwhelming results I got from the 13 inch XPSS 1TB drive. Wi-Fi speeds were excellent and it comes with the AX1650 Wi-Fi 6 chip. When I first heard the sound from the speakers I was like wow, they're really nice. They are very loud, have nice stereo separation and the speakers face up so you will have no degradation in sound quality when using it on your laptop. Have a listen. After using it side by side with the MacBook Pro 16 speakers though, I thought well, these are some of the best speakers on a laptop that I've heard but they don't reproduce the same range of sound as the MacBook Pro 16. Base was not existent and the highest sound in muddy. That being said, the mid range where vocals are was phenomenally clear. Overall, these are in the top 5% of laptop speakers that I've tested but they aren't number one. The MacBook Pro 16 still retains that crown. Audio latency on this laptop was excellent. The best score I've ever got on a PC laptop, I literally ran a code compile while the latency test was running and I could not get it to falter. Here I am testing the webcam in excellent lighting conditions. This is how it looks and sounds. The fingerprint reader worked well as did Windows Hello facial recognition. The charger is small for 130W and uses USB type C. The laptop would not charge off the smaller 13 inch Dell XPS's 45 watt charger though which is odd as the MacBook Pro 16 does charge off it. Keep in mind for light usage I found this laptop's processor only draws 5W to 25W of power so this should have worked and would have been handy. It does charge off the MacBook Pro 16's 96 watt charger though. Battery life for light usage like browsing the web and writing the script was around 7 hours with the screen dimmed by 3 notches on this model's 86 watt battery which is pretty good. I'd assume you could get more with a lower resolution screen if you dimmed the brightness more than I did. I had no blue screens or crashes during my time with this laptop. However, I did have one complete lock up when I plugged in a fairly standard Anker USB C to Ethernet adapter. I had to hold down the power button for a long time to force a restart. Not only this but others are reporting many issues that I have either encountered myself in this laptop or the 13 inch XPS 9300. For example the screen auto dimming even though all auto dimming settings are disabled. High pitch fan noise, the laptop occasionally freezing and the screen going black for a couple of seconds when you plug in the power. This last one viewers have told me is caused by the HDR setting that you can turn off but it really shouldn't happen to begin with. Overall though, I personally found these issues occurred less on my 15 inch XPS than on the 13 but moral of the story is this there are risks associated with purchasing this laptop. So I would only buy it from a seller where you have a no hassle 30 day return period so you can probably try the laptop to ensure you don't have the faulty trackpad and you can handle the other issues. Now apologies folks because I'll be returning this laptop due to the trackpad issue I didn't want to open it up to show you the internals. That being said I did some research and apparently the SSD is user upgradable and so is the RAM. And lastly it is very competitively priced compared to the MacBook Pro 16. At the time I made this video the laptop was priced at $299. The equivalent MacBook Pro 16 retails for $2,799 but it does include the 8 core processor. However as I showed you it doesn't perform that much better. And if you go for a 32 gig of RAM model with a 2 terabyte SSD the price difference balloons to almost $1,000. So let me wrap up I really like this laptop a lot. I think it is an excellent competitor to the MacBook Pro 16 and other high laptops. I like the keyboard better than the MacBook Pro, it has an SD card reader, it has WiFi 6 and if you do any gaming this is the winner as it can play modern games in decent settings. The reason I choose the MacBook Pro 16 over this is if you like Mac OS you want that slightly bigger screen, better sound and a cooler feeling chassis. For most people though I'd save the money and get this so long as you get one with a working trackpad. This laptop is really just great at everything and is my new all-round recommendation for a power user. Well that's all for today folks if you like this video you know what to do, smash that subscribe button, yes smash it, hit the thumbs up and the notification bell until next time I will catch you later.
