titulo: MacBook Air M4 vs M3: What’s New in Apple’s Latest Update?
transcricao: Hey folks, Apple's latest iteration of the MacBook Air, the M4 model, brings a series of improvements over its predecessor, the M3. While at first glance, many aspects of the two models remain the same, the M4 introduces key upgrades that enhance performance, efficiency, and overall usability. The design and form factor of the MacBook Air M4 remain unchanged, retaining the ultra-slime chassis, liquid retina display, and the same selection of ports, including mag-safe charging, two Thunderbolt 4 ports, and a headphone jack. The laptop is still available in two sizes, 13-inch and 15-inch, and Apple has introduced a new Sky Blue color, alongside the existing silver, starlight and midnight options. A minor yet notable upgrade is the addition of center stage to the webcam, which ensures users stay in the center of the frame during video calls. One of the most significant changes in the MacBook Air M4 is its pricing. The base model now starts at £999, which is £100 cheaper than the MacBook Air M3's initial price. Apple's decision to lower the entry price aligns with the air's original positioning as an affordable and popular choice, particularly among students who can purchase it with an additional £100 discount. Under the hood, the MacBook Air M4 features Apple's new M4 processor, marking a major performance leap. The chip has up to 10 CPU cores, consisting of four performance cores and six efficiency cores, compared to the M3's 8-core configuration with four performance and four efficiency cores. The M4 also features a 10-core GPU as standard, an increase from the base 8-core GPU in the M3 model, offering improved graphics performance. Moreover, the M4 processor is built on TSMC's second-generation 3nm process, compared to the first-generation 3nm process used for the M3, delivering better efficiency and power management. A major advancement in the M4 is its neural processing unit, which plays a crucial role in Apple intelligence features. The M4's 16-core NPU can process up to 38 trillion operations per second, a significant improvement over the M3's 16-core NPU, which could handle 18 trillion operations per second. This enhancement enables faster machine learning and AI-driven tasks, making the MacBook Air M4 a more future-proof option for users who rely on AI-powered applications. Apple has also increased the memory capacity of the MacBook Air M4, unlike the M3, which originally started with 8GB of RAM, but later shifted to 16GB. The M4 standard model begins with 16GB of unified memory. Additionally, users can now configure the M4 with up to 32GB of RAM, a jump from the M3's maximum of 24GB. This change is particularly beneficial for users running multiple resource-intensive applications, narrowing the gap between the MacBook Air and the MacBook Pro lineup. Another notable improvement is external display support. The MacBook Air M4 can now power two external 6K displays simultaneously while keeping its built-in display active. Meanwhile, the ASUS Vivo Book 16 is a budget-friendly productivity laptop running on a Snapdragon X processor, offering Windows 11 ARM performance with a larger screen. This comparison will examine their design, display quality, hardware, battery performance, pricing and overall value. The MacBook Air M4 continues Apple's tradition of sleek and minimalist aesthetics, boasting a lightweight aluminum chassis and an ultra-thin profile. The introduction of the new Sky Blue color adds a fresh look to the lineup. Setting it apart from previous models. Despite its thin design, the MacBook Air M4 maintains a premium build quality, making it one of the most stylish laptops available. The ASUS Vivo Book 16 on the other hand takes a more practical approach, featuring an all-plastic body that helps keep costs down. While it is not as refined as the MacBook Air, it remains durable and includes military grave drop protection. However, at 1.88 kilograms, it is noticeably heavier and chunkier than Apple's offering. The keyboard is comfortable but lacks backlighting, which may be a drawback for some users. Apple's MacBook Air M4 features a 15-inch liquid retina display with excellent color accuracy, sharp resolution and high brightness levels. The screen delivers true-to-life visuals, making it ideal for creative professionals and multimedia consumption. Additionally, the display supports wide color gamuts and high contrast ratios, ensuring an immersive experience. In contrast, the ASUS Vivo Book 16 has a 16-inch display with a 1200-P resolution and a 16-10 aspect ratio. While its anti-glare coating helps reduce reflections, the panel only achieves around 260 nits of brightness, lower than the advertised 300 nits. Color accuracy is also limited, covering about 60% of the Adobe RGB spectrum. The MacBook Air M4 is powered by Apple's latest M4 chip, which provides noticeable improvements in power efficiency and processing capabilities. The M4 chip enhances multitasking, handles video editing with ease, and offers significant battery life gains. The MacBook Air also includes faster SSD speeds and the ability to support two external monitors, a first for the air lineup. Its 12 megapixels ultra-wide front camera, with center stage ensures high quality video calls. The ASUS Vivo Book 16 is equipped with a Snapdragon X processor, 16GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD. While it handles everyday tasks like web browsing and document editing smoothly, its integrated Adreno GPU underperforms compared to Apple's M4 graphics. This makes it less suitable for GPU intensive tasks, such as gaming and professional video editing. Windows 11 ARM provides a decent experience, but some applications, like Adobe Premier Pro, run in emulation mode, leading to performance issues. The Vivo Book 16 does have a solid port selection, including HDMI 2.1, USB-C, USB-A, and a headphone jack, which gives it an advantage over the MacBook Air's limited port options. Apple's M4 chip is optimized for power efficiency, leading to outstanding battery performance. In a controlled test, a 10 minute 4K video export used only 1% battery, whereas the previous M3 model consumed 4%. In real-world usage, the MacBook Air M4 consistently outlasts its predecessors, making it one of the best choices for users needing all day battery life. The ASUS Vivo Book 16 benefits from ARM architecture, which provides steady battery performance, even when unplugged. However, its battery life does not match that of the MacBook Air M4. While it offers decent longevity for a Windows laptop, users looking for the longest lasting battery should favor Apple's machine. Ultimately, choosing between the two depends on individual needs. If you require a high performance, long-lasting laptop, with a premium design, the MacBook Air M4 is the better option. If budget constraints are a primary concern and you mainly need a laptop for productivity tasks, the ASUS Vivo Book 16 offers good value for its price. titulo: MacBook Air M4 vs MacBook Air M1 | Is It Finally Time to Upgrade?
transcricao: Hey folks, Apple has unveiled the new MacBook Air M4. Five years after introducing the first MacBook Air powered by Apple Silicon, this launch raises an important question for those still using the MacBook Air M1. Is it time to upgrade? While we have yet to fully test the MacBook Air M4, the MacBook Air M1 was a revolutionary device that earned a flawless five-star rating upon its release. Understanding the key differences between the two models can help determine whether the upgrade is worthwhile. The MacBook Air M4 is available for purchase from Apple and authorized retailers with the 13-inch model starting at £999 and the 15-inch model at £1,199. The MacBook Air M1, while no longer sold directly by Apple, is still available through third-party retailers, often in refurbished condition. One of the most significant differences between these models is the processor. The MacBook Air M1, launched in 2020, introduced Apple's custom M1 chip, revolutionising performance and efficiency in ultra-portable laptops. The MacBook Air M4, on the other hand, boasts the latest M4 chip, which Apple claims is up to twice as fast as the M1. With a powerful 10-core CPU, up to 10-core GPU, and support for up to 32 gigabytes of unified memory, the M4 chip is designed for greater efficiency and performance. Apple also states that the M4's neural engine is up to three times faster than the M1, which should enhance AI-driven applications. According to Apple, the MacBook Air M4 is 1.6 times faster at performing tasks such as spreadsheet calculations in Microsoft Excel, and up to twice as fast for video editing in iMovie and Adobe Photoshop. While we have not yet independently verified these claims, our past experience with the MacBook Air M1 showed it to be an incredibly capable machine, exceeding expectations for a first-generation Apple Silicon product. Audio performance is another area where the MacBook Air M4 has seen improvements. While the MacBook Air M1 delivered decent stereo sound with Dolby Atmos support, Apple has upgraded the M4 with a 4-speaker system, capable of creating a three-dimensional soundstage for movies and music. The new model also supports spatial audio and dynamic headtracking when using compatible air pods. The webcam has also received a significant upgrade. The MacBook Air M4 features a 12 megapixels camera capable of 1080p HD video recording, which is particularly useful for frequent video calls and meetings. The inclusion of center stage technology ensures users remain in frame, while the new desk perspective feature provides an overhead view of the user's workspace. In contrast, the MacBook Air M1 720p camera was often criticized for looking washed out and struggling in low light conditions. One advantage of the MacBook Air M4 is the availability of both 13-inch and 15-inch models. Offering flexibility for different users. The 13-inch model remains lightweight at 1.24kg, making it an excellent option for portability, while the 15-inch version provides additional screen space for multitasking. The MacBook Air M1, in contrast, is only available in a single 13-inch size. Although both devices are marketed as 13-inch models, the M4 actually features a slightly larger 13.6-inch display due to thinner bezels, whereas the M1 retains a 13.3-inch screen. The MacBook Air M1 comes with an IPS LED backlit display, with a peak brightness of 400 nits, which we found to be sufficient for most use cases. The MacBook Air M4, however, upgrades to a liquid retina display, with a slightly higher resolution of 250060 by 160064 pixels, and a peak brightness of 500 nits. While these are welcome improvements, neither MacBook Air model supports Apple's pro-motion technology or refresh rates beyond 60Hz. Those looking for a smoother display experience would need to consider the MacBook Pro M4. For users still using the MacBook Air M1, the decision to upgrade depends on specific needs. Given the M1's excellent performance, continued Apple intelligence support, and our original 5-star rating, it remains a highly capable machine even today. However, the MacBook Air M4 offers compelling reasons to upgrade, including a faster processor, better camera, improved audio, and a more immersive display. As soon as we get our hands on the new MacBook Air M4, we will provide a more detailed assessment to determine whether Apple's claims hold up in real-world usage. titulo: Surface Laptop 13 vs Surface Laptop 7 | Which Copilot+ PC Wins?
transcricao: Hey folks, on May 6, 2025, Microsoft officially unveiled a new member of its surface line-up. A 13-inch surface laptop designed as part of its next-generation, co-pilot plus PC family. As it enters the scene, it sits next to the more established surface laptop 7, 2024, sparking a necessary conversation about what's gained and what's lost. At a glance, the 2025 model appears sleeker, more affordable, and purpose built for portability. But a deeper inspection reveals several compromises that may limit its appeal compared to its predecessor. The first thing to note is the price difference. The new 13-inch surface laptop launches at $899, making it $100 cheaper than the Surface Laptop 7's original base price of $999, though the older model is often found for less during sales. However price alone doesn't tell the full story. Display quality is a significant differentiator. The surface laptop 7 features a 13.8-inch screen with a sharp 2,304x1536 resolution, a smooth 120 hertz refresh rate, and a 1,400-1,536 pixel density 1 contrast ratio. In comparison, the new 13-inch model drops to a lower 1920 by 1280 resolution, a standard 60 hertz refresh rate, and a less vivid 1000-1 contrast ratio. This downgrade not only affects visual crispness and motion fluidity, but also the immersive quality that users may expect from a premium surface device. Despite the display setback, Microsoft leans into portability with the 2025 release. It is the thinnest and lightest surface laptop ever, weighing just 1.22 kilograms and measuring 15.6mm thick. The surface laptop 7, in contrast, weighs 1.43kg and is 17.5mm thick. These are not insignificant reductions and could make the new model attractive to students or professionals constantly on the move. However, the move to a smaller single size display option in the 2025 model marks a reduction in variety. The surface laptop 7 was available in both 13.8-inch and 15-inch sizes. On the performance front, the story is more complex. The 2025 surface laptop uses an 8-core Snapdragon X-plus processor with a maximum of 16GB RAM. In contrast, the surface laptop 7 could be configured with a more powerful 10-core Snapdragon X-plus, or even the 12-core Snapdragon X Elite, and supported up to 64GB of LPDDR5 RAM. From a performance standpoint, the new model is clearly a step down. Users needing higher compute power or future-proofing via RAM capacity will likely find the surface laptop 7 more attractive. In terms of authentication, the surface laptop 7 again has the upper hand, offering a full HD webcam with Windows Hello facial recognition. Microsoft opted to strip down the biometric features in the 2025 model, offering only a fingerprint sensor embedded in the power button. This may be seen as a regression in convenience and security. Charging and port design also sees a shift. The 2025 model drops the surface connect port in favour of standard USB-C charging, aligning it with broader industry trends, but potentially disappointing surface loyalists who favoured the magnetic connector. Battery life, on the other hand, is an area where the new model makes a strong showing. Microsoft claims up to 16 hours of web browsing and 23 hours of local video playback. Outpacing the surface laptop 7's 13 hours of browsing and 20 hours of video, this improvement could significantly enhance productivity for those working unplugged throughout the day. In summary, the new 13-inch surface laptop, 2025, is a slimmer, lighter and more affordable addition to the surface family, bringing co-pilot plus PC features and excellent battery life to the forefront. However, it makes several trade-offs to achieve this. Display quality, processor power, RAM capacity and authentication features all take a hit when compared to the surface laptop 7. For casual users prioritising portability and battery life, the 2025 model may be enough, but for power users, creatives or professionals, the surface laptop 7 still holds more value, especially when it can be found at discounted prices. Until we complete in-depth testing, it's hard to recommend the new model as a full successor rather than a lighter entry level alternative. Thanks for watching, what do you think about this comparison? Write your opinion in the comments, have a nice day and God bless you.

titulo: Microsoft Surface Pro 12 vs iPad Pro | Which One Fits your Workflow?
transcricao: Hey folks, Microsoft has officially unveiled its newest dual-purpose device, the 12-inch Surface Pro, positioning it as a creative companion, designed for typing, writing and drawing all on one machine. Naturally, it invites comparison with Apple's iPad Pro M4, which is known for its premium features and outstanding performance. While the Surface Pro is still awaiting full hands-on reviews, its specs and design choices offer enough information to draw an early comparison with Apple's top tier tablet. In terms of pricing, the Surface Pro enters the market at a more accessible level. The 12-inch model starts at £799, while the iPad Pro begins at a significantly higher £9999 for the 11-inch model and rises to £1299 for the 13-inch variant. The internal hardware powering each device reveals a philosophical split between the two companies. Microsoft's Surface Pro runs on Qualcomm's Snapdragon X Plus chip, which is part of the new wave of AI-ready processors boasting 45 tops of NPU performance. This classifies the Surface Pro as a co-pilot plus PC, designed to fully support Microsoft's AI toolset. Though we haven't tested this chip in a tablet yet, similar hardware and laptops has shown it to be competent for both light and intensive tasks. On the other side, the iPad Pro M4 is powered by Apple's latest M4 chip, derived from the same silicon family used in high-end Macs. The performance here is tried and tested, with real-world results that demonstrate dominance over mobile-class chips, including older Qualcomm models. Apple's own AI tools, Apple Intelligence, are seamlessly integrated thanks to the M4's neural engine, and everyday use feels incredibly smooth and responsive. Design-wise, the Surface Pro leans into versatility, it features a built-in 165-degree kickstand, making it a true two-in-one device that can easily switch between laptop mode and tablet use, without the need for additional accessories. The iPad Pro, while incredibly sleek and elegant, doesn't include this kind of functionality out of the box, requiring a separate case or keyboard for a similar experience. In terms of display technology, Apple takes a clear lead. The iPad Pro M4 features a tandem OLED panel, what Apple calls the ultra-retina XDR, that delivers stunning brightness up to 1000 nits for SDR content and rich deep-color reproduction. Our review called it one of the best displays available on any tablet, especially for HDR video. The Surface Pro's 12-inch model, by contrast, comes with a standard LCD, at a resolution of 2196, by 1464 and peaks at just 400 nits. Only the more expensive 13-inch Surface Pro model upgrades to OLED. Furthermore, the iPad Pro's 120Hz promotion refresh rate enhances fluidity, while the Surface Pro tops out at a still smooth, but lesser 90Hz. In the area of portability, Apple has created its thinnest and lightest iPad Pro yet. The 13-inch model is just 5.1mm thick, and weighs 579 grams. Thanks largely to its OLED display that does away with the need for a backlight. The Surface Pro, while dubbed Microsoft's thinnest and lightest co-pilot plus PC, still measures 7.8mm thick, and weighs 686 grams, making it slightly bulkier and heavier in comparison. Overall, both the Surface Pro and the iPad Pro M4 aim to be more than casual tablets. They're designed as productivity machines capable of real work, with pro grade processes and AI capabilities. The Surface Pro carves out a unique place with its integrated kickstand, Windows ecosystem, and relatively lower starting price, making it a compelling option for those looking for a flexible and affordable 2-in-1 device. However, the iPad Pro M4 excels in display quality, raw performance, and overall refinement, especially for users already invested in the Apple ecosystem. Until we can fully review the Surface Pro, it's hard to declare a definitive winner, but it's clear that Microsoft has built a product that on paper, stands as a strong rival to Apple's premium tablet, especially for users looking for the functionality of a laptop with the form factor of a tablet. Would you prioritize the lower price and built-in flexibility of the Surface Pro, or the sheer power and elegance of the iPad Pro M4? titulo: MacBook Pro M5 vs M4 | Apple’s Subtle Yet Powerful Upgrade!
transcricao: Hey folks, the latest addition to Apple's premium laptop lineup, the MacBook Pro M5, aims to refine an already impressive formula established by its predecessor, the MacBook Pro M4. Both devices share much of the same DNA, from their sleek aluminum unibody construction to their liquid retina XDR displays, but the M5 introduces a new chip set, and some subtle internal improvements that hinted Apple's continued focus on performance, AI integration and efficiency. At launch, the MacBook Pro M5 is priced at £1599 for the 14-inch base model and £2499 for the 16-inch variant. Aligning with Apple's typical premium pricing, it officially releases on October 22nd. The MacBook Pro M4, which debuted in May 2024, is now harder to find directly from Apple, but remains available through third-party retailers like Amazon, typically starting around £1999 for higher-capacity versions. The biggest and most consequential difference between the two models lies in the chip set. Apple's new M5 chip is being positioned as a leap forward in AI and graphics capabilities. The company claims the M5's next-generation 10-core GPU delivers up to 1.6 times faster graphics performance, and up to 3.5 times greater AI processing power than the M4, thanks to a re-engineered architecture and a 16-core neural engine, optimized for Apple intelligence, the company's suite of on-device generative AI features. This upgrade means tasks like image generation, contextual writing assistance, and real-time translation, will execute more smoothly and securely, as all processing happens locally, rather than in the cloud. However, it's worth remembering that the M4 remains an extremely capable chip. During its review cycle, it was widely praised for offering excellent everyday performance, fluid multitasking, and robust thermals. While the M4 may not match the M5's raw AI throughput, it's still more than sufficient for most creative, professional and productivity tasks, particularly in the M4 Pro or M4 Max configurations that offered extended GPU cores and memory bandwidth. For most users, M4 continues to deliver a top-tier MacBook experience. Both the M5 and M4 fully support Apple intelligence features, such as Genmoji, image playground, and writing tools, which help users rephrase text or generate images on the fly. The difference is in responsiveness and local model handling. The M5 is built to process AI workloads faster, particularly when running local LLMS, which ties directly into Apple's improvements to internal storage. The M5 supports up to four terabytes of SSD capacity, and boasts twice the read-slash right speed of the M4, ensuring rapid app loading and file access, while the M4 maxes out at two terabytes of storage. Despite the improved internal hardware, battery life remains consistent across both models. Apple claims up to 24 hours of video playback or typical web use on a single charge, an impressive figure that has been maintained for several generations. In real-world usage, MacBook Pro M4 comfortably delivered around 12 hours of active multitasking performance, and M5 is expected to achieve similar results, given its comparable power envelope and efficiency tuning. Both laptops support fast charging when paired with a 96 watt power adapter or higher, but Apple's decision not to include a charger with M5 feels like a regression. Buyers will need to purchase a 70 or 96 watt adapter separately. Visually, the two laptops are nearly identical, the same 14.2-inch liquid retina XDR display remains in both. With up to 1,000 nits of sustained brightness, and 1,600 nits in HDR content. Both models can also be configured with an optional Nano Texture Glass finish for 150 pounds more. Reducing glare and adding a paper-like matte effect that dramatically improves usability in bright environments. The consistency here isn't a sign of stagnation, but rather a reflection of Apple's confidence in its display technology, which remains among the best in the industry. For anyone using an older Intel-based MacBook, or even an M2 or M3 generation model however, the M5 offers a clear leap in performance, efficiency, and AI integration. It represents Apple's continued refinement of its silicon ecosystem, and its strategic move toward a future where on-device intelligence plays a central role in the Mac OS experience. Ultimately, the MacBook Pro M5 continues Apple's pattern of steady thoughtful evolution rather than dramatic overhaul. It's a machine designed not to surprise, but to perfect. A hallmark of a product line that has long defined professional laptop excellence. For new buyers or those coming from older MacBook generations, it's an excellent choice. For current M4 owners however, patients might pay off until Apple unveils something truly transformative. Thanks for watching. What do you think about the new comparison? Cooling is one of the areas where Samsung has made meaningful generational improvements, and it also helps separate the Pro from the Ultra. For the first time, the Galaxy Book 6 Pro includes a vapor chamber, which should allow it to manage heat more evenly and maintain performance under heavier workloads than previous Pro models. In terms of design, both laptops feel premium, but they approach it differently. The Galaxy Book 6 has undergone a noticeable redesign compared to earlier Samsung notebooks with new proportions, revised angles, and a much more cohesive overall look. The centered keyboard and touchpad immediately improve ergonomics and give the laptop a more balanced appearance. The M4 MacBook Air by contrast is intentionally familiar. The thin aluminum body remains one of the lightest and most comfortable laptops to carry around, and the overall build quality is still among the best in the industry. The display is one of the clearest points of separation between these two laptops. The M4 MacBook Air sticks with a traditional LCD display running at 60Hz. It is sharp, color accurate, and more than good enough for everyday work, but it lacks the visual punch and smoothness found on Samsung's higher refresh panels. Hardware philosophy is where the biggest contrast emerges. The Galaxy Book 6 is built around Intel's core ultra-processors, offering strong CPU performance with improved efficiency compared to previous generations. In higher configurations, it can also scale up dramatically with Intel Arc graphics, or even dedicated Nvidia R-TXGPRs, turning it into a surprisingly capable machine for creative workloads and even some gaming. The M4 MacBook Air relies on Apple's custom silicon, and the M4 chip is exceptionally efficient. Despite being passively cooled with no fan, it delivers fast responsive performance for everyday tasks and short bursts of heavier work. Video editing, photo processing, and multitasking feel effortless, even if sustained heavy workloads eventually hit thermal limits. Camera quality is increasingly important, and both laptops have improved here. Battery life is a strong point for both machines, but they achieve it in different ways. Thanks to Apple's silicon and a slightly larger battery, it delivers consistently long battery life, often stretching beyond a full day for lighter workloads. While Samsung has closed the gap, Apple still holds a slight advantage in predictable, all-day endurance, without performance compromises, choosing between the Samsung Galaxy Book 6 and the M4 MacBook Air ultimately comes down to priorities. The Galaxy Book 6 is the more versatile and visually striking machine, offering higher refresh rate displays, optional touch screen and amlled technology, broader port selection, and configurations that can scale into serious performance territory. The M4 MacBook Air meanwhile remains the definition of balance. It is quiet, extremely efficient, powerful for its size, and now more affordable with a much better base memory configuration. It doesn't push boundaries in design or display technology, but it delivers a consistently excellent experience that is hard to fault. Both feature a sturdy, all-metal chassis, an integrated kickstand, and a detachable keyboard that connects via Pogo pins or Bluetooth. The 2025 model already felt like a mature and practical design compared to earlier dual-screen laptops, offering a more cohesive setup than competitors. The 2026 version refines this even further with improved materials and tighter tolerances. Its seroluminum chassis feels lighter, more durable, and more resistant to fingerprints and scratches, while the hinge and kickstand feels slightly more solid and flush. The displays are where the ZenBook Duo identity truly shines, and this is also where the 2026 model makes one of its biggest leaps. The ZenBook Duo 2026 takes that experience further, with dual 14-inch Lumen-Apro displays across the lineup, maintaining the same 3K resolution, but increasing the refresh rate to 144Hz. The anti-reflective coating on the 2026 model is also more effective, making glare less of an issue under strong lighting compared to the 2025 version. Under the hood, the difference between the two generations is substantial. The ZenBook Duo 2025 is powered by Intel's Core Ultra 9285H AeroLake processor, which delivers excellent single core and multi-core performance, and pairs with Intel ARK140T integrated graphics. The ZenBook Duo 2026 upgrades to Intel's Core Ultra X9 Series 3 Panther-Lake processor, bringing a stronger CPU, a more capable integrated ARK-B Series GPU, and a dramatically improved NPU. With support for higher sustained power levels and faster LPDDR5X memory, the 2026 model feels effortlessly smooth even when both displays are heavily loaded with demanding applications. Camera hardware is similar on both devices, with each featuring a 1080p IR camera that supports Windows Hello Face recognition. Thanks to the more powerful NPU in the ZenBook Duo 2026, AI-powered features like eye contact correction, noise reduction, and background effects run more efficiently and smoothly, particularly during multitasking scenarios where the 2025 model can occasionally feel more taxed. Battery life is another area where the ZenBook Duo 2026 clearly pulls ahead. The ZenBook Duo 2025 is equipped with a 75 watt-hours battery, which already delivers respectable endurance for a dual OLED laptop. The ZenBook Duo 2026 upgrades to a much larger 99 watt-hours battery, and the real-world results are impressive. Even with both displays active, it can push past 12 hours of mixed use, including streaming, productivity, and creative work. This makes the 2026 model far more reliable for all-day use without constantly worrying about charging, especially when combined with improved battery management tools in the My ASUS app and the included 100 watt fast charger. Both the ASUS ZenBook Duo 2025 and ZenBook Duo 2026 are excellent examples of how dual-screen laptops can be genuinely useful rather than gimmicky. The 2025 model remains a strong option, offering great performance, flexible display configurations, and solid battery life, particularly if you opt for the full HD plus panels and value efficiency. The ZenBook Duo 2026, however, represents a clear generational upgrade. It feels like the most complete and confident version of the ZenBook Duo yet. HP equips the Elitebook 8G1A with a display available in both 14-inch and 16-inch sizes. The standard resolution is 1920x1200, with brightness options ranging from 300 to 400 nits, and up to 800 nits in configurations that include HP's SureView privacy filter. There is also a higher-end 2.5K 120Hz panel option. The anti-glare coating is particularly useful in office and travel environments, reducing reflections under bright lighting. The M5 MacBook Pro offers a 14.2-inch liquid retina XDR mini LED display, with a 3024 by 1964 resolution and ProMotion 120Hz refresh rate. This panel delivers exceptional brightness, deep contrast, and outstanding color accuracy. While HP emphasizes privacy and practicality, Apple focuses on visual excellence and creative precision. After the hood, the Elitebook 8G1A runs on AMD Ryzen AI 7 Pro 350, or Ryzen 7 250 processors, offering up to 8 cores. It supports up to 64 gigs of DDR5 memory via SODIM slots, allowing for future upgrades, and PCIe Gen 4 NVMe storage up to 2 terabytes. It radiates on 780M or 860M graphics, handle display, and light creative workloads. A key highlight is the dedicated NPU capable of delivering up to 50 tops of AI performance, enabling local AI processing for co-pilot and HP's AI companion tools. The M5 MacBook Pro uses Apple's M5 chip with a 10 core CPU, 10 core GPU, and 16 core neural engine. It relies on unified memory architecture, configurable from 16 up to 32 gigs, and extremely fast PCIe Gen 5 SSD storage up to 4 terabytes. Unlike the HP, memory is not user-upgradable, but the unified architecture allows CPU and GPU to share memory efficiently, improving performance per watt. In single core and many multi-core workloads, the M5 demonstrates exceptional performance, often surpassing comparable X86 processors. Battery life is an area where both laptops perform strongly, though with different strengths. The Elite Book 8G1A includes a 62 watt hours battery and delivers reliable all-day performance under mixed business workloads. HP's battery management tools, including smart sense and fastchart support, help maintain battery health and quickly restore power to 50% in about 30 minutes. The M5 MacBook Pro pushes efficiency further. Rated for up to 24 hours of video playback, it consistently delivers exceptional endurance thanks to Apple's silicon's power efficiency. Even under demanding workloads, the MacBook tends to maintain longer unplugged usage than many Windows competitors. Combined with silent or near-silent operation under light tasks, the MacBook Pro sets a high standard for performance per watt and battery longevity. Although the choice depends on use case and ecosystem preference, organizations deeply invested in Windows infrastructure and enterprise security frameworks will likely find the Elite Book 8G1A better aligned with their needs. Individual professionals and creatives seeking top-tier efficiency, display quality, and seamless hardware software integration may gravitate toward the M5 MacBook Pro. Both laptops stand at the forefront of their respective platforms, demonstrating how competition between ARM-based Apple silicon and advanced X86 systems continues to push the industry forward. titulo: MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air M5 | What’s the Difference?
transcricao: Hey folks, the introduction of the MacBook Neo marks a significant shift in Apple's laptop strategy, offering a far more affordable entry point into the Mac ecosystem. For years, the MacBook Air M5 and its predecessors have been considered the default starting point for most people looking to buy a Mac laptop. With the Neo launching at just $599, Apple is clearly targeting students, casual users, and budget buyers who may have previously found the company's laptops out of reach. One of the most striking contrasts between the two machines lies in their processors. The MacBook Neo is powered by the Apple A18 Pro chip, the same mobile processor found in the iPhone 16 Pro and iPhone 16 Pro Max. This is an unusual move for a laptop, because Apple traditionally uses its M-series chips, which are designed specifically for desktop and laptop workloads. Despite being a smartphone chip, Apple claims the A18 Pro can deliver impressive performance, including speeds up to 50% faster than certain mainstream PCs with Intel Core Ultra 5 processors when handling everyday tasks. The MacBook Air M5, however, operates in a completely different performance tier. It runs on the new Apple M5 chip, a processor specifically engineered for laptops and desktops. The M5 features a 10 core CPU at a 10 core GPU, giving it considerably more computational power for demanding workloads. Just like video editing, software development, high-resolution photo processing, and heavier multitasking, will almost certainly run smoother on the air. Display options also highlight the difference in positioning between these two laptops. The MacBook Neo is available in a single 13-inch configuration, making it the smallest and simplest MacBook currently offered. This compact size will appeal to people who prioritize portability and want a lightweight machine for school, travel, or everyday use. The MacBook Air M5 by contrast comes in two sizes, a 13.6-inch model, and a larger 15.3-inch version. The larger screen offers more workspace for multitasking, and provides a more immersive experience for media consumption or light gaming. Camera performance is another area where the MacBook Air M5 holds a clear advantage. The air features a 12 megapixel camera with center stage technology, a system that automatically keeps users centered during video calls as they move. The MacBook Neo instead uses the older 1080p FaceTime HD camera design. Memory and storage options further reinforce the difference between a budget laptop and a premium ultra portable. The MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB of RAM, which is sufficient for light multitasking, but may become restrictive over time as software demands increase. Storage options are also modest, starting at 256GB and going up to 512GB. The MacBook Air M5 starts with 16GB of RAM, double the base memory of the Neo, and can be configured with up to 24GB or even 32GB for demanding professional workloads. Conactivity is fairly similar between the two devices, though there are some technical differences. The MacBook Air M5 includes two Thunderbolt 4 ports, headphone jack, and Apple's MagSafe charging connector. Thunderbolt 4 provides very high transfer speeds and support for advanced peripherals, such as high resolution external displays and fast storage devices. The MacBook Neo offers a nearly identical physical layout with two USB-C ports, a headphone jack, and MagSafe charging, but the USB-C ports are more limited. Pricing is perhaps the most important difference between these two laptops. With a starting price of $599, the MacBook Neo is dramatically cheaper than the MacBook Air M5, which begins at $1,099. Ultimately, the MacBook Neo and MacBook Air M5 are designed for very different audiences. The Neo focuses on affordability and accessibility, giving users a simple way to enter the Mac ecosystem without spending over $1,000. The Air M5 continues to represent Apple's premium thin and light laptop experience, delivering higher performance and more advanced features for those willing to pay the extra cost. If Apple's performance claims about the A18 Pro hold true in real-world testing, the MacBook Neo could quickly become one of the most popular budget laptops available, while the MacBook Air M5 will remain the better choice for users who need more power and flexibility from their machine. titulo: MacBook Air M5 vs MacBook Pro M5 | Which One Should You Pick?
transcricao: Hey folks, the launch of the MacBook Air M5 alongside the MacBook Pro M5 marks an interesting moment in Apple's laptop lineup. Because for the first time in this generation, both machines are powered by the same underlying silicon. At first glance, the MacBook Air M5 continues the philosophy that has defined the air series for years. It focuses on portability, efficiency, and minimalism, while still delivering impressive performance. Starting at around $1,099, it positions itself as one of the most accessible ways to enter Apple's modern laptop ecosystem. The MacBook Pro M5, on the other hand, starts at $16.99 and is only available in the more restrained finishes of space, black, and silver. Its design language immediately communicates that it is intended for more demanding users. The Pro sits between the air sizes, with a 14-inch chassis, and while it is the heaviest device in the lineup, at roughly 1.55 kg, the difference in weight is not extreme. Still, if mobility is the top priority, the air models clearly have the advantage. The 13-inch air weighs about 1.23 kg, making it one of the lightest full power laptops Apple has ever produced, and incredibly easy to carry around throughout the day. As both laptops share the M5 processor, the fundamental computing experience is expected to be very similar. Apple positions the M5 as a major step forward in efficiency and everyday computing performance. Whether you are handling typical productivity tasks, running creative applications, editing photos, or even working with moderate video projects, the M5 is designed to offer fast and responsive performance without sacrificing battery life. Our feature both machines benefit from is the integration of Apple's latest software ecosystem powered by the M5 architecture. The chip enables the full set of Apple intelligence tools, bringing enhanced on-device AI features, improved multitasking efficiency, and smarter system optimizations across Mac OS. Where the MacBook Pro begins to distinguish itself more clearly is in battery life and charging capabilities. Apple claims the MacBook Pro M5 can reach up to 16 hours of web browsing and as much as 24 hours of video streaming, which is extremely impressive, even by Apple's already high standards. The MacBook Air is also strong in this department, promising around 15 hours of web use and up to 18 hours of video playback, but the Pro still manages to stretch further. In addition, the MacBook Pro supports faster charging when connected to a 96 watt power adapter or higher, while the MacBook Air tops out at 70 watts. Connectivity is another area where the differences become noticeable. The MacBook Air follows Apple's minimalist design philosophy with a limited but clean port selection. It offers two Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports, a MagSafe charging connector, and a 3.5mm headphone jack. For everyday users, this setup is usually sufficient, but anyone dealing with cameras, external displays, or additional peripherals may find it restrictive. The MacBook Pro expands the connectivity significantly. In addition to the same ports found on the air, it adds a third Thunderbolt 4 port, an HDMI port, and a full-size SDXC card reader. One of the most compelling advantages of the MacBook Pro lies in its display technology. The MacBook Air uses Apple's liquid retina display, which already offers excellent color accuracy, support for the P3 wide color gamut, true tone technology, and a brightness level of up to 500 nits. For everyday tasks like browsing, editing documents, and even creative work, it is a very good screen. However, the MacBook Pro pushes things much further with its liquid retina XDR panel. This display supports dramatically higher brightness levels, reaching up to 1600 nits for HDR content, which makes highlights look incredibly vivid when watching movies or working with HDR video. The resolution is also higher at 3,024x1964 pixels, providing extremely sharp visuals across the 14-inch panel. Ultimately, the comparison between the MacBook Air M5 and the MacBook Pro M5 highlights Apple's strategy of offering two machines that share the same core performance but target very different users. The MacBook Air M5 is clearly designed for portability, affordability, and everyday versatility. It delivers the power of the M5 chip in a thin and lightweight design, making it ideal for students, travelers, remote workers, and anyone who values mobility above all else. For many users, the MacBook Air M5 will likely provide everything they need at a significantly lower cost, making it arguably the better value in Apple's lineup. But for those who require the best display, expanded connectivity, and the ability to sustain performance under heavy workloads, the MacBook Pro M5 remains the more powerful and capable machine, despite sharing the same processor. On paper, the A18 Pro inside the MacBook Neo sounds impressive. Apple claims substantial gains in everyday tasks and especially in AI-related workloads thanks to its 16-core neural engine. For lighter usage such as browsing, document editing, media consumption, and even some casual creative work, the Neo could feel extremely fast and responsive. The MacBook Air M1, despite its age, remains one of the most well-balanced laptops Apple has ever made. Powered by the M1 ship, it delivers a level of performance that was groundbreaking at launch and is still very capable today. The combination of an 8-core CPU and integrated GPU allows it to handle demanding applications with consistency and its fan-list design manages to maintain impressive efficiency without excessive throttling. Display quality is another area where the MacBook Neo attempts to modernize the experience. Port selection is also generous on both devices, something that's becoming rare and thin laptops. However, the A16 gains an extra advantage with the inclusion of an SD card reader, which is particularly useful for creators working with photos and videos. The display is where the differences become far more pronounced. Both laptops use OLED panels, so you're getting deep blacks and vibrant colors, regardless of which model you choose. However, the ZenBook A16 elevates the experience with a higher 3K resolution and a smoother 120Hz refresh rate, making everything from scrolling to media consumption noticeably more fluid and detailed. It also reaches higher brightness levels, which improves visibility in brighter environments. The A14 still delivers excellent color accuracy and visual quality, even slightly edging out the A16 and Adobe RGB coverage, but its lower resolution and 60Hz refresh rate make it feel more conventional by comparison. Performance is another area where the A16 pulls ahead, thanks to its more powerful Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme processor, compared to the standard Snapdragon X2 Elite in the A14. In real-world usage, both machines handle daily tasks effortlessly, from multitasking to media editing and even light gaming. However, the A16 has more headroom for demanding workloads and maintains smoother performance under pressure. That said, both devices still face the broader limitations of ARM-based Windows systems, including occasional compatibility issues with certain software. Battery life is one of the most impressive aspects of both laptops, reinforcing their focus on mobility. The ZenBook A14 stands out with exceptional endurance, lasting well over 22 hours in testing, which makes it ideal for users who prioritize long stretches away from a charger. The A16, while slightly behind, still offers excellent longevity at around 19 hours, which is more than enough for multiple work days. Ultimately, the choice between the ZenBook A14 and A16 comes down to priorities, rather than a simple question of which is more advanced. The ZenBook A16 is the more capable and feature rich device, offering a superior display, stronger performance, and a slightly more versatile design, making it the better option for power users and those who value a larger screen. On the other hand, the A14 excels in portability, battery efficiency, and value, making it a fantastic choice for students, travelers, or anyone who needs a lightweight yet powerful everyday laptop. So while size is the most visible difference, it's far from the only one. The A16 represents a step up in performance and display technology, whereas the A14 focuses on delivering a balanced, ultra-portable experience without sacrificing too much power.
